test("intent rate limiting spans processes via the database and fails open on database errors", async () => {
  const intentsSource = await readFile(new URL("../src/storage/upload-intents.ts", import.meta.url), "utf8");
  const inMemoryIndex = intentsSource.indexOf("intentRateLimiter.allow(userId)");
  const databaseIndex = intentsSource.indexOf("recordMediaIntentRateHit(userId)");
  assert.ok(inMemoryIndex >= 0, "the in-process window remains the always-available guard");
  assert.ok(databaseIndex > inMemoryIndex, "the durable database window is consulted after the in-process check");
  assert.match(intentsSource, /mcp_media_intent_rate_hits/);
  assert.match(intentsSource, /hit_at > NOW\(\) - make_interval\(secs => \$2\)/);
  assert.match(intentsSource, /media_upload_intent_rate_limit_database_unavailable/,
    "a database error must fail open instead of blocking uploads");
});

// --- Expired-upload cleanup through the reference-counted helper --------------

test("expired uploads are cleaned up through the reference-counted storage helper", async () => {
  const intentsSource = await readFile(new URL("../src/storage/upload-intents.ts", import.meta.url), "utf8");
  assert.match(intentsSource, /await deleteUnreferencedStorageObjects\(candidates\)/,
    "sweeping never deletes an object without the shared reference check");
  const selectIndex = intentsSource.indexOf("SELECT id, storage_path, kind");
  const cleanupIndex = intentsSource.indexOf("deleteUnreferencedStorageObjects(candidates)");
  const rowIndex = intentsSource.indexOf("storage_path IS NULL OR id = ANY($2::text[])");
  assert.ok(selectIndex >= 0 && cleanupIndex > selectIndex, "candidates are read before the reference-counted delete");
  assert.ok(rowIndex > cleanupIndex, "rows whose object survived the sweep are kept for retry");
  const sharedStorage = await readFile(new URL("../src/scheduler.ts", import.meta.url), "utf8");
  assert.match(sharedStorage, /export async function deleteUnreferencedStorageObjects/,
    "the sweeper reuses the exact reference-counted deletion helper");
  assert.match(sharedStorage, /export interface StorageCleanupResult/);
});

// --- Failed-attempt throttling (HTTP 429) --------------------------------------

test("failed-attempt penalty box blocks after the limit and slides with the window", () => {
  const box = intents.createSlidingWindowPenaltyBox({ maxAttempts: 3, windowMs: 1000 });
  assert.equal(box.blocked("ip-a", 0), false);
  box.record("ip-a", 0);
  box.record("ip-a", 10);
  box.record("ip-a", 20);
  assert.equal(box.blocked("ip-a", 30), true);
  assert.equal(box.blocked("ip-a", 40), true, "blocking consults the recorded history without adding a hit");
  assert.equal(box.blocked("ip-b", 40), false, "blocks are per client address");
  assert.equal(box.blocked("ip-a", 1050), false, "the penalty window has slid past all recorded failures");
});

test("the upload endpoint throttles failed attempts before any claim and records every rejection", async () => {
  const source = await readFile(new URL("../src/media/upload-endpoint.ts", import.meta.url), "utf8");
  assert.match(source, /Too many failed upload attempts/);
  assert.match(source, /media_upload_throttled/);
  assert.match(source, /windowMs: 600_000/);
  const blockedIndex = source.indexOf("attemptPenalty.blocked(clientKey)");
  const claimIndex = source.indexOf("claimPendingMediaUploadIntent(token)");
  const arrayBufferIndex = source.indexOf("request.arrayBuffer()");
  assert.ok(blockedIndex >= 0 && blockedIndex < claimIndex, "throttling rejects requests before any intent claim");
  assert.ok(claimIndex < arrayBufferIndex, "the single-use claim still precedes byte transfer");
  const recordCalls = source.match(/attemptPenalty\.record\(clientKey\)/g) ?? [];
  assert.ok(recordCalls.length >= 4, "bad tokens, rejected payloads, unknown intents, and failures all count");
  const endpoint = await readFile(new URL("../src/config/env.ts", import.meta.url), "utf8");
  assert.match(endpoint, /mediaUploadAttemptLimit = integer\("MEDIA_UPLOAD_ATTEMPT_LIMIT", "30", 1\)/);
});

import assert from "node:assert/strict";
import test from "node:test";
import { waitForInstagramContainer } from "../src/platforms/meta.js";

async function withInstagramStatuses<T>(
  statuses: string[],
  run: () => Promise<T>,
): Promise<{ result: T; requests: number }> {
  const originalFetch = globalThis.fetch;
  let requests = 0;
  globalThis.fetch = async (_input: RequestInfo | URL): Promise<Response> => {
    const status = statuses[requests++];
    if (!status) throw new Error("Unexpected additional Instagram status request.");
    return Response.json({ status_code: status });
  };
  try {
    return { result: await run(), requests };
  } finally {
    globalThis.fetch = originalFetch;
  }
}

test("publishing waits until Instagram reports the container is finished", async () => {
  const { requests } = await withInstagramStatuses(["IN_PROGRESS", "FINISHED"], () =>
    waitForInstagramContainer("container-id", "access-token"),
  );
  assert.equal(requests, 2);
});

test("Instagram container processing errors fail before publish", async () => {
  await withInstagramStatuses(["ERROR"], () =>
    assert.rejects(waitForInstagramContainer("container-id", "access-token"), /status ERROR/),
  );
});

import assert from "node:assert/strict";
import { createCipheriv, randomBytes } from "node:crypto";
import { mkdtemp, readFile, rm, writeFile } from "node:fs/promises";
import { tmpdir } from "node:os";
import { join } from "node:path";
import test from "node:test";

import type { StoredToken } from "../src/platforms/types.js";

const directory = await mkdtemp(join(tmpdir(), "social-media-mcp-multiuser-"));
const tokenFile = join(directory, "tokens.enc");
process.env["SOCIAL_MCP_TOKEN_FILE"] = tokenFile;
process.env["SOCIAL_MCP_TOKEN_ENCRYPTION_KEY"] = "a".repeat(64);
process.env["TOKEN_STORE_BACKEND"] = "local";
process.env["MCP_OWNER_USER_ID"] = "local-owner";

const tokenStore = await import("../src/auth/token-store.js");
const { config } = await import("../src/config/env.js");

test.after(async () => rm(directory, { recursive: true, force: true }));

const instagramToken: StoredToken = {
  accessToken: "alice-instagram",
  scopes: ["instagram_business_basic"],
  connectedAt: 1,
};
const linkedinToken: StoredToken = {
  accessToken: "bob-linkedin",
  scopes: ["w_member_social"],
  connectedAt: 2,
};

function writeLegacyVault(payload: unknown): string {
  const key = Buffer.from(process.env["SOCIAL_MCP_TOKEN_ENCRYPTION_KEY"]!, "hex");
  const iv = randomBytes(12);
  const cipher = createCipheriv("aes-256-gcm", key, iv);
  const ciphertext = Buffer.concat([cipher.update(JSON.stringify(payload), "utf8"), cipher.final()]);
  return JSON.stringify({
    version: 1,
    iv: iv.toString("hex"),
    tag: cipher.getAuthTag().toString("hex"),
    ciphertext: ciphertext.toString("hex"),
  });
}

test("local token vault isolates each user's credentials", async () => {
  await tokenStore.saveLocalTokens("alice", { instagram: instagramToken });
  await tokenStore.saveLocalTokens("bob", { linkedin: linkedinToken });

  assert.equal((await tokenStore.loadTokens("alice")).instagram?.accessToken, "alice-instagram");
  assert.equal((await tokenStore.loadTokens("alice")).linkedin, undefined);
  assert.equal((await tokenStore.loadTokens("bob")).linkedin?.accessToken, "bob-linkedin");
  assert.equal((await tokenStore.loadTokens("bob")).instagram, undefined);
  assert.deepEqual(await tokenStore.loadTokens("carol"), {});
});

test("legacy single-user vaults are adopted by the configured owner identity", async () => {
  await writeFile(tokenFile, writeLegacyVault({ linkedin: { ...linkedinToken, accessToken: "legacy-linkedin" } }));

  assert.equal((await tokenStore.loadTokens(config.ownerUserId)).linkedin?.accessToken, "legacy-linkedin");
  assert.deepEqual(await tokenStore.loadTokens("someone-else"), {});
});

});

import assert from "node:assert/strict";
import { readFile } from "node:fs/promises";
import test from "node:test";

import {
  InMemoryOAuthSessionStore,
  buildFrontendRedirectUrl,
  expectedPlatformsForCallbackPath,
  hashOAuthState,
  isOAuthCallbackPath,
  type CreateOAuthSessionInput,
} from "../src/auth/oauth-sessions.js";
import { processOAuthCallback } from "../src/auth/oauth.js";

function sessionInput(overrides: Partial<CreateOAuthSessionInput> = {}): CreateOAuthSessionInput {
  return {
    sessionId: "session-1",
    state: "state-1",
    userId: "user-1",
    platform: "linkedin",
    redirectUri: "https://social-media-cloud-worker.onrender.com/oauth/linkedin/callback",
    expiresAt: Date.now() + 60_000,
    ...overrides,
  };
}

test("maps callback paths to their expected platforms", () => {
  assert.deepEqual(expectedPlatformsForCallbackPath("/oauth/meta/callback"), ["facebook", "instagram"]);
  assert.deepEqual(expectedPlatformsForCallbackPath("/oauth/linkedin/callback"), ["linkedin"]);
  assert.equal(expectedPlatformsForCallbackPath("/worker/run"), null);
  assert.equal(expectedPlatformsForCallbackPath("/health"), null);
  assert.equal(isOAuthCallbackPath("/oauth/meta/callback?state=abc"), true);
  assert.equal(isOAuthCallbackPath("/oauth/linkedin/callback"), true);
  assert.equal(isOAuthCallbackPath("/health"), false);
  assert.equal(isOAuthCallbackPath(undefined), false);
});

test("builds a fixed allowlisted frontend redirect and refuses unsafe bases", () => {
  assert.equal(
    buildFrontendRedirectUrl("https://app.example.com/", "connected", "linkedin"),
    "https://app.example.com/accounts?oauth=connected&platform=linkedin",
  );
  assert.equal(
    buildFrontendRedirectUrl("https://app.example.com", "failed"),
    "https://app.example.com/accounts?oauth=failed",
  );
  assert.equal(buildFrontendRedirectUrl("", "failed"), null);
  assert.equal(buildFrontendRedirectUrl("   ", "failed"), null);
  assert.equal(buildFrontendRedirectUrl("javascript:alert(1)", "failed"), null);
  assert.equal(buildFrontendRedirectUrl("ftp://example.com", "failed"), null);
  assert.equal(buildFrontendRedirectUrl("https://user:pass@example.com", "failed"), null);
  // A path or host supplied elsewhere can never move the redirect off /accounts.
  const injected = buildFrontendRedirectUrl("https://app.example.com/accounts", "failed", "facebook");
  assert.equal(injected, "https://app.example.com/accounts?oauth=failed&platform=facebook");
});

test("hashes OAuth state deterministically without keeping the raw value", () => {
  const hash = hashOAuthState("super-secret-state");
  assert.match(hash, /^[0-9a-f]{64}$/);
  assert.equal(hash, hashOAuthState("super-secret-state"));
  assert.notEqual(hash, hashOAuthState("super-secret-state-2"));
});

test("in-memory store claims a state exactly once", async () => {
  const store = new InMemoryOAuthSessionStore();
  await store.create(sessionInput({ sessionId: "once", state: "once-state", userId: "u1" }));

  const first = await store.claim("once-state", ["linkedin"]);
  assert.equal(first.claimed, true);
  if (first.claimed) assert.equal(first.session.redirectUri, "https://social-media-cloud-worker.onrender.com/oauth/linkedin/callback");

  const second = await store.claim("once-state", ["linkedin"]);
  assert.equal(second.claimed, false);
  if (!second.claimed) assert.equal(second.reason, "used");
});

test("in-memory store rejects expired states", async () => {
  const store = new InMemoryOAuthSessionStore();
  await store.create(sessionInput({ sessionId: "expired", state: "expired-state", expiresAt: Date.now() - 1 }));

  const result = await store.claim("expired-state", ["linkedin"]);
  assert.equal(result.claimed, false);
  if (!result.claimed) assert.equal(result.reason, "expired");

  const status = await store.getStatus("expired", "user-1");
  assert.equal(status.status, "expired");
});

test("in-memory store rejects wrong-platform states without consuming them", async () => {
  const store = new InMemoryOAuthSessionStore();
  await store.create(sessionInput({
    sessionId: "fb",
    state: "fb-state",
    userId: "u2",
    platform: "facebook",
    redirectUri: "https://social-media-cloud-worker.onrender.com/oauth/meta/callback",
  }));

  const wrong = await store.claim("fb-state", ["linkedin"]);
  assert.equal(wrong.claimed, false);
  if (!wrong.claimed) assert.equal(wrong.reason, "wrong_platform");

  const right = await store.claim("fb-state", ["facebook", "instagram"]);
  assert.equal(right.claimed, true);
  if (right.claimed) assert.equal(right.session.platform, "facebook");
});

test("in-memory store isolates authorization sessions by authenticated user", async () => {
  const store = new InMemoryOAuthSessionStore();
  await store.create(sessionInput({ sessionId: "iso", state: "iso-state", userId: "alice" }));

  await assert.rejects(() => store.getStatus("iso", "bob"), /not found or expired/i);
  await assert.rejects(() => store.waitForStatus("iso", "bob", 0), /not found or expired/i);

  const status = await store.getStatus("iso", "alice");
  assert.equal(status.status, "pending");
});

test("in-memory store wakes waiters when the callback completes", async () => {
  const store = new InMemoryOAuthSessionStore();
  await store.create(sessionInput({ sessionId: "wait", state: "wait-state", userId: "carol" }));

  const waiting = store.waitForStatus("wait", "carol", 5);
  await store.updateStatus("wait", "connected");
  const resolved = await waiting;
  assert.equal(resolved.status, "connected");
});

test("callback marks a provider cancellation without attempting an exchange", async () => {
  const store = new InMemoryOAuthSessionStore();
  await store.create(sessionInput({ sessionId: "cancel", state: "cancel-state", userId: "dave" }));
  let finishCalled = false;

  const outcome = await processOAuthCallback(
    new URLSearchParams({ state: "cancel-state", error: "access_denied" }),
    ["linkedin"],
    { store, finish: async () => { finishCalled = true; } },
  );

  assert.equal(outcome.result, "cancelled");
  assert.equal(finishCalled, false);
  assert.equal((await store.getStatus("cancel", "dave")).status, "cancelled");
});

test("callback fails safely when the authorization code is missing", async () => {
  const store = new InMemoryOAuthSessionStore();
  await store.create(sessionInput({ sessionId: "nocode", state: "nocode-state", userId: "erin" }));

  const outcome = await processOAuthCallback(
    new URLSearchParams({ state: "nocode-state" }),
    ["linkedin"],
    { store, finish: async () => { throw new Error("should not run"); } },
  );

  assert.equal(outcome.result, "failed");
  assert.equal((await store.getStatus("nocode", "erin")).status, "failed");
});

test("callback records a failed exchange without leaking secrets or codes", async () => {
  const store = new InMemoryOAuthSessionStore();
  await store.create(sessionInput({ sessionId: "fail", state: "fail-state", userId: "frank" }));

  const outcome = await processOAuthCallback(
    new URLSearchParams({ state: "fail-state", code: "auth-code-123" }),
    ["linkedin"],
    {
      store,
      finish: async () => {
        throw new Error("client_secret=super-secret&access_token=abc123 failed for authorization_code=auth-code-123");
      },
    },
  );

  assert.equal(outcome.result, "failed");
  const status = await store.getStatus("fail", "frank");
  assert.equal(status.status, "failed");
  const recorded = status.error ?? "";
  assert.match(recorded, /\[redacted\]/);
  assert.doesNotMatch(recorded, /super-secret/);
  assert.doesNotMatch(recorded, /abc123/);
  assert.doesNotMatch(recorded, /auth-code-123/);
});

test("callback rejects an unknown state and a reused state", async () => {
  const store = new InMemoryOAuthSessionStore();
  const unknown = await processOAuthCallback(new URLSearchParams({ state: "nope" }), ["linkedin"], {
    store,
    finish: async () => undefined,
  });
  assert.equal(unknown.result, "failed");

  await store.create(sessionInput({ sessionId: "reuse", state: "reuse-state", userId: "gina" }));
  const first = await processOAuthCallback(new URLSearchParams({ state: "reuse-state", code: "c1" }), ["linkedin"], {
    store,
    finish: async () => undefined,
  });
  assert.equal(first.result, "connected");
  const second = await processOAuthCallback(new URLSearchParams({ state: "reuse-state", code: "c2" }), ["linkedin"], {
    store,
    finish: async () => undefined,
  });
  assert.equal(second.result, "failed");
});

FILE: social-media-mcp/tests/remote-media-input.test.ts

import assert from "node:assert/strict";
import test from "node:test";
import { REMOTE_MEDIA_HINT, rejectRemoteLocalPaths } from "../src/tools/media-input.js";

// Verified behavior (MCP specification + modelcontextprotocol discussion #1197):
// tool arguments are JSON and the published protocol has no client-to-server
// file-upload primitive. Claude.ai therefore cannot hand the Render worker image
// bytes or a readable local path. Remote tools must accept only HTTPS URLs.

test("remote mode rejects imagePath before any filesystem read", () => {
  assert.throws(
    () => rejectRemoteLocalPaths(true, { imagePath: "/etc/passwd" }),
    /imagePath[\s\S]*remote MCP/i,
  );
});

test("remote mode rejects documentPath", () => {
  assert.throws(
    () => rejectRemoteLocalPaths(true, { documentPath: "C:\\secrets\\report.pdf" }),
    /documentPath[\s\S]*remote MCP/i,
  );
});

test("remote mode rejects any media[].path", () => {
  assert.throws(
    () => rejectRemoteLocalPaths(true, { mediaPaths: [undefined, "/etc/shadow"] }),
    /media\[\]\.path[\s\S]*remote MCP/i,
  );
});

test("remote mode accepts URL-only media arguments", () => {
  assert.doesNotThrow(() => rejectRemoteLocalPaths(true, {}));
  assert.doesNotThrow(() => rejectRemoteLocalPaths(true, {
    imagePath: undefined,
    documentPath: undefined,
    mediaPaths: [undefined, undefined],
  }));
});

test("local stdio mode keeps local file support", () => {
  assert.doesNotThrow(() => rejectRemoteLocalPaths(false, {
    imagePath: "/tmp/image.png",
    documentPath: "/tmp/document.pdf",
    mediaPaths: ["/tmp/image.png", "/tmp/video.mp4"],
  }));
});

test("remote rejection points callers at the HTTPS upload fallback", () => {
  assert.throws(
    () => rejectRemoteLocalPaths(true, { imagePath: "/etc/passwd" }),
    (error: unknown) => {
      const message = error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error);
      return message.includes("HTTPS") && /upload/i.test(message) && message.includes(REMOTE_MEDIA_HINT);
    },
  );
});

import assert from "node:assert/strict";
import test from "node:test";
import { isPrivateIpAddress, resolvePublicHttpsUrl } from "../src/utils/remote-media.js";

test("rejects private, loopback, link-local, and reserved IP addresses", () => {
  for (const address of [
    "0.0.0.0",
    "10.1.2.3",
    "100.64.0.1",
    "127.0.0.1",
    "169.254.1.1",
    "172.16.5.4",
    "192.0.0.1",
    "192.168.1.1",
    "198.18.0.1",
    "224.0.0.1",
    "255.255.255.255",
    "::",
    "::1",
    "fc00::1",
    "fe80::1",
    "ff02::1",
    "2001:db8::1",
    "::ffff:10.0.0.1",
    "not-an-ip",
  ]) {
    assert.equal(isPrivateIpAddress(address), true, `${address} should be rejected`);
  }
  for (const address of ["8.8.8.8", "1.1.1.1", "2606:4700:4700::1111"]) {
    assert.equal(isPrivateIpAddress(address), false, `${address} should be allowed`);
  }
});

test("resolves only public HTTPS media URLs", async () => {
  await assert.rejects(() => resolvePublicHttpsUrl("http://example.com/a.jpg"), /HTTPS/);
  await assert.rejects(() => resolvePublicHttpsUrl("https://user:pass@example.com/a.jpg"), /credentials/);
  await assert.rejects(() => resolvePublicHttpsUrl("https://localhost/a.jpg"), /publicly reachable/);
  await assert.rejects(() => resolvePublicHttpsUrl("https://127.0.0.1/a.jpg"), /private|reserved|loopback/);
  await assert.rejects(() => resolvePublicHttpsUrl("not-a-url"), /absolute URL/);

  const target = await resolvePublicHttpsUrl("https://8.8.8.8/media/a.jpg");
  assert.equal(target.address, "8.8.8.8");
  assert.equal(target.hostname, "8.8.8.8");
  assert.equal(target.url.toString(), "https://8.8.8.8/media/a.jpg");
});

test("rejects SSRF targets before any outbound request", async () => {
  for (const url of [
    "https://10.0.0.1/media/a.jpg",
    "https://172.16.0.1/media/a.jpg",
    "https://192.168.0.5/media/a.jpg",
    "https://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/",
    "https://127.0.0.1/media/a.jpg",
    "https://[::1]/media/a.jpg",
    "https://[fe80::1]/media/a.jpg",
    "https://localhost/media/a.jpg",
    "http://example.com/media/a.jpg",
    "https://user:pass@example.com/media/a.jpg",
  ]) {
    await assert.rejects(() => resolvePublicHttpsUrl(url), /HTTPS|credentials|publicly reachable|private|reserved|loopback/);
  }
});

test("accepts a public HTTPS image URL", async () => {
  const target = await resolvePublicHttpsUrl("https://8.8.8.8/media/image.png");
  assert.equal(target.url.protocol, "https:");
  assert.equal(target.address, "8.8.8.8");
});

import assert from "node:assert/strict";
import { readFile } from "node:fs/promises";
import test from "node:test";

// Regression guard: every remote media tool must reject local paths, and the
// only local filesystem read in the tool layer must sit behind that guard.

test("all remote media tools call the local-path guard", async () => {
  const register = await readFile(new URL("../src/tools/register.ts", import.meta.url), "utf8");

  const guardCalls = register.match(/rejectRemoteLocalPaths\(remote/g) ?? [];
  assert.equal(
    guardCalls.length,
    3,
    "social_publish, social_schedule_posts, and social_schedule_media must each call the guard",
  );

  for (const field of ["imagePath", "documentPath", "mediaPaths"]) {
    assert.match(register, new RegExp(field), `${field} must be passed to the guard`);
  }
});

test("the only tool-level readFile sits after the remote path guard", async () => {
  const register = await readFile(new URL("../src/tools/register.ts", import.meta.url), "utf8");

  const readFileCalls = register.match(/await readFile\(/g) ?? [];
  assert.equal(readFileCalls.length, 1, "only the stdio media[].path branch may read a file");

  const guardIndex = register.indexOf("rejectRemoteLocalPaths(remote, { documentPath, mediaPaths");
  const readFileIndex = register.indexOf("await readFile(item.path)");
  assert.ok(guardIndex >= 0, "the media tool guard must be present");
  assert.ok(readFileIndex > guardIndex, "readFile must run only after the remote path guard");
});

FILE: social-media-mcp/tests/schedule-text-only.test.ts

import assert from "node:assert/strict";
import { mkdtemp, readFile } from "node:fs/promises";
import { createServer } from "node:net";
import { tmpdir } from "node:os";
import { dirname, join, resolve } from "node:path";
import { fileURLToPath } from "node:url";
import test from "node:test";
import { Client } from "@modelcontextprotocol/client";
import { StdioClientTransport } from "@modelcontextprotocol/client/stdio";

// A tool result body parsed from the stdio client's first text content block.
function resultBody(result: { content: Array<{ type: string; text?: string }> }): Record<string, unknown> {
  return JSON.parse(String(
    result.content[0]?.type === "text" ? result.content[0].text : "{}",
  )) as Record<string, unknown>;
}

async function availablePort(): Promise<number> {
  const server = createServer();
  await new Promise<void>((resolve, reject) => {
    server.once("error", reject);
    server.listen(0, "127.0.0.1", resolve);
  });
  const address = server.address();
  if (!address || typeof address === "string") throw new Error("Could not determine a free test port.");
  await new Promise<void>((resolve, reject) => {
    server.close((error) => error ? reject(error) : resolve());
  });
  return address.port;
}

async function readFileText(relativePath: string): Promise<string> {
  return readFile(new URL(relativePath, import.meta.url), "utf8");
}

test("scheduler accepts optional images and stores text-only rows with no media", async () => {
  const scheduler = await readFileText("../src/scheduler.ts");

  assert.match(scheduler, /export async function schedulePosts\(/);
  assert.match(scheduler, /image\?: string \| NewScheduledImage/);
  assert.match(scheduler, /mediaType: document \? "document" : imageInput \? "image" : "none"/);
  assert.match(scheduler, /contentType: imageInput \? contentType : "application\/octet-stream"/);
  // Text-only is rejected for Instagram at scheduling time, before tokens/DB.
  assert.match(scheduler, /if \(!imageInput && post\.platform === "instagram"\)/);
  assert.match(scheduler, /Instagram requires an image reference; text-only posts are not supported\./);
  // Local tunnel requirement applies only when an image reference is present.
  assert.match(scheduler, /if \(imageInput && config\.scheduledImageStorage === "local"/);
});

test("publishing handles text-only jobs through the existing platform publishers", async () => {
  const scheduler = await readFileText("../src/scheduler.ts");
  const meta = await readFileText("../src/platforms/meta.ts");
  const linkedin = await readFileText("../src/platforms/linkedin.ts");

  // The no-image branches call the text-only platform publishers directly.
  assert.match(scheduler, /result = await publishLinkedIn\(job\.userId, job\.text\);/);
  assert.match(scheduler, /result = await publishMeta\(job\.userId, job\.platform as MetaPlatform, job\.text, undefined\);/);
  // Facebook publishes text-only posts to the Page feed; Instagram still needs a URL.
  assert.match(meta, /message: text \?\? ""/);
  assert.match(meta, /Instagram publishing requires a publicly reachable HTTPS image URL\./);
  // LinkedIn text-only posts use the Posts API without media.
  assert.match(linkedin, /export async function publishLinkedIn\(ownerId: string, text\?: string, imagePath\?: string/);
});

test("social_schedule_posts accepts at most one image reference and no image is valid", async () => {
  const register = await readFileText("../src/tools/register.ts");

  assert.match(register, /Provide at most one of imageUrl, imageStoragePath, or imagePath\./);
  assert.doesNotMatch(register, /Provide exactly one of imageUrl, imageStoragePath, or imagePath\./);
  // The image variable may be undefined and is passed through as-is.
  assert.match(register, /let image: string \| NewScheduledImage \| undefined;/);
  assert.match(register, /await schedulePosts\(userId, posts, image, document\)/);
  // Descriptions document the text-only behavior and the Instagram exception.
  assert.match(register, /omit every image reference for a text-only Facebook or LinkedIn post; Instagram always requires an image/);
});

test("built MCP server schedules text-only posts without an image", async () => {
  const projectRoot = resolve(dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)), "..");
  const callbackPort = await availablePort();
  const tokenFile = join(await mkdtemp(join(tmpdir(), "social-mcp-text-only-")), "tokens.enc");
  const transport = new StdioClientTransport({
    command: process.execPath,
    args: ["dist/index.js"],
    cwd: projectRoot,
    stderr: "pipe",
    // Deterministic settings: the token vault is an empty temp file, and
    // dotenv never overrides an explicitly exported value, so real .env cloud
    // backends are ignored. DATABASE_URL stays configured because the stdio
    // server initializes the scheduler store at startup; the "not connected"
    // token check below throws before any row would be inserted.
    env: {
      ...process.env,
      OAUTH_CALLBACK_PORT: String(callbackPort),
      SOCIAL_MCP_TOKEN_FILE: tokenFile,
      SUPABASE_URL: "",
      SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY: "",
      TOKEN_STORE_BACKEND: "local",
      SCHEDULED_IMAGE_STORAGE: "local",
      SCHEDULER_MODE: "local",
      OAUTH_CALLBACK_MODE: "local",
    },
  });
  const client = new Client({ name: "social-media-mcp-text-only-test", version: "1.0.0" });
  let serverStderr = "";
  transport.stderr?.setEncoding("utf8");
  transport.stderr?.on("data", (chunk) => { serverStderr += chunk; });

  try {
    await client.connect(transport);
    const scheduledAt = new Date(Date.now() + 3_600_000).toISOString();

    // A text-only Facebook post passes image validation and reaches the token
    // check ("not connected"), proving no image is required before scheduling.
    const facebook = await client.callTool({
      name: "social_schedule_posts",
      arguments: {
        posts: [{ platform: "facebook", scheduledAt, text: "Text-only validation" }],
      },
    });
    assert.equal(facebook.isError, undefined);
    const facebookBody = resultBody(facebook);
    assert.equal(facebookBody.success, false);
    assert.match(String(facebookBody.error), /facebook is not connected; authorize it before scheduling/);

    // LinkedIn behaves identically for text-only posts.
    const linkedin = await client.callTool({
      name: "social_schedule_posts",
      arguments: {
        posts: [{ platform: "linkedin", scheduledAt, text: "Text-only validation" }],
      },
    });
    const linkedinBody = resultBody(linkedin);
    assert.equal(linkedinBody.success, false);
    assert.match(String(linkedinBody.error), /linkedin is not connected; authorize it before scheduling/);

    // Instagram keeps its image requirement for scheduled posts.
    const instagram = await client.callTool({
      name: "social_schedule_posts",
      arguments: {
        posts: [{ platform: "instagram", scheduledAt, text: "Text-only validation" }],
      },
    });
    const instagramBody = resultBody(instagram);
    assert.equal(instagramBody.success, false);
    assert.match(String(instagramBody.error), /Instagram requires an image reference/);

    // Two image references are still rejected to catch ambiguous input.
    const ambiguous = await client.callTool({
      name: "social_schedule_posts",
      arguments: {
        posts: [{ platform: "facebook", scheduledAt, text: "Text-only validation" }],
        imageUrl: "https://127.0.0.1:9/unreachable.png",
        imageStoragePath: "scheduled/local-owner/" + "0".repeat(64) + ".png",
      },
    });
    const ambiguousBody = resultBody(ambiguous);
    assert.equal(ambiguousBody.success, false);
    assert.match(String(ambiguousBody.error), /Provide at most one of imageUrl, imageStoragePath, or imagePath\./);
  } catch (error) {
    throw new Error(`stdio test failed: ${String(error)}; server stderr: ${serverStderr}`, { cause: error as Error });
  } finally {
    await client.close();
  }
});

import assert from "node:assert/strict";
import { createServer, type Server } from "node:http";
import { mkdtemp, rm, writeFile } from "node:fs/promises";
import os from "node:os";
import path from "node:path";
import test from "node:test";
import {
  validateScheduledImage,
  validateScheduledImageWithRetries,
} from "../src/utils/scheduled-image.js";

const imageToken = "a".repeat(64);
const jpegBytes = Buffer.from([0xff, 0xd8, 0xff, 0xe0, 0x00, 0x10, 0x4a, 0x46, 0x49, 0x46]);

async function fixture(): Promise<{ imagePath: string; cleanup: () => Promise<void> }> {
  const directory = await mkdtemp(path.join(os.tmpdir(), "scheduled-image-test-"));
  const imagePath = path.join(directory, "image.jpg");
  await writeFile(imagePath, jpegBytes);
  return { imagePath, cleanup: () => rm(directory, { recursive: true, force: true }) };
}

async function startServer(handler: (server: Server) => void): Promise<{ baseUrl: string; close: () => Promise<void> }> {
  const server = createServer();
  handler(server);
  await new Promise<void>((resolve, reject) => {
    server.once("error", reject);
    server.listen(0, "127.0.0.1", resolve);
  });
  const address = server.address();
  if (!address || typeof address === "string") throw new Error("Could not determine test server port.");
  return {
    baseUrl: `http://127.0.0.1:${address.port}`,
    close: () => new Promise<void>((resolve, reject) => {
      server.close((error) => error ? reject(error) : resolve());
    }),
  };
}

function imageResponse(bytes: Uint8Array = jpegBytes, contentType = "image/jpeg", status = 200): Response {
  return new Response(bytes, { status, headers: { "content-type": contentType } });
}

test("validates the local route and dynamically configured public image URL", async () => {
  const file = await fixture();
  const requestedUrls: string[] = [];
  try {
    const validation = await validateScheduledImage({
      imagePath: file.imagePath,
      imageToken,
      contentType: "image/jpeg",
      checkPublic: true,
      localBaseUrl: "http://127.0.0.1:43127",
      publicBaseUrl: "https://changed-tunnel.example",
      fetcher: async (input) => {
        requestedUrls.push(String(input));
        return imageResponse();
      },
    });
    assert.equal(validation.valid, true);
    assert.equal(validation.local.status, 200);
    assert.equal(validation.local.bytes, jpegBytes.byteLength);
    assert.equal(validation.public?.valid, true);
    assert.deepEqual(requestedUrls, [
      `http://127.0.0.1:43127/scheduled-media/${imageToken}`,
      `https://changed-tunnel.example/scheduled-media/${imageToken}`,
    ]);
  } finally {
    await file.cleanup();
  }
});

test("reports an incorrect local image-server port as a retryable connection failure", async () => {
  const file = await fixture();
  const unused = await startServer((server) => {
    server.on("request", (_request, response) => response.end());
  });
  await unused.close();
  try {
    const validation = await validateScheduledImage({
      imagePath: file.imagePath,
      imageToken,
      contentType: "image/jpeg",
      checkPublic: false,
      localBaseUrl: unused.baseUrl,
      timeoutMs: 1000,
    });
    assert.equal(validation.valid, false);
    assert.equal(validation.retryable, true);
    assert.match(validation.error ?? "", /connection refused|request failed/i);
  } finally {
    await file.cleanup();
  }
});

test("detects an image route 404 and does not inspect the public tunnel", async () => {
  const file = await fixture();
  const requestedUrls: string[] = [];
  try {
    const validation = await validateScheduledImage({
      imagePath: file.imagePath,
      imageToken,
      contentType: "image/jpeg",
      checkPublic: true,
      localBaseUrl: "http://127.0.0.1:43128",
      publicBaseUrl: "https://old-tunnel.example",
      fetcher: async (input) => {
        requestedUrls.push(String(input));
        return new Response("<html>Not found</html>", {
          status: 404,
          headers: { "content-type": "text/html" },
        });
      },
    });
    assert.equal(validation.valid, false);
    assert.equal(validation.local.status, 404);
    assert.equal(validation.retryable, false);
    assert.match(validation.error ?? "", /HTTP 404/);
    assert.equal(requestedUrls.length, 1);
  } finally {
    await file.cleanup();
  }
});

test("rejects HTML, invalid MIME types, and empty image bodies", async () => {
  const file = await fixture();
  try {
    for (const [response, expected] of [
      [new Response("<html>ngrok error</html>", { headers: { "content-type": "text/html" } }), /invalid image MIME type/],
      [imageResponse(jpegBytes, "image/webp"), /invalid image MIME type/],
      [imageResponse(Buffer.alloc(0)), /empty image response/],
      [imageResponse(Buffer.from("<html>error</html>")), /not valid image\/jpeg image data/],
    ] as const) {
      const validation = await validateScheduledImage({
        imagePath: file.imagePath,
        imageToken,
        contentType: "image/jpeg",
        checkPublic: false,
        localBaseUrl: "http://127.0.0.1:43129",
        fetcher: async () => response.clone(),
      });
      assert.equal(validation.valid, false);
      assert.match(validation.error ?? "", expected);
    }
  } finally {
    await file.cleanup();
  }
});

test("bounds image response size and identifies request timeouts", async () => {
  const file = await fixture();
  try {
    const oversized = await validateScheduledImage({
      imagePath: file.imagePath,
      imageToken,
      contentType: "image/jpeg",
      checkPublic: false,
      localBaseUrl: "http://127.0.0.1:43130",
      maxBytes: 5,
      fetcher: async () => imageResponse(),
    });
    assert.match(oversized.error ?? "", /exceeds the configured 5-byte size limit/);
    assert.equal(oversized.retryable, false);

    const timeout = await validateScheduledImage({
      imagePath: file.imagePath,
      imageToken,
      contentType: "image/jpeg",
      checkPublic: false,
      localBaseUrl: "http://127.0.0.1:43131",
      fetcher: async () => { throw new DOMException("Timed out", "TimeoutError"); },
    });
    assert.match(timeout.error ?? "", /timed out/i);
    assert.equal(timeout.retryable, true);
  } finally {
    await file.cleanup();
  }
});

test("retries temporary tunnel failures with exponential backoff and stops after recovery", async () => {
  const file = await fixture();
  let publicRequests = 0;
  const delays: number[] = [];
  try {
    const result = await validateScheduledImageWithRetries(
      {
        imagePath: file.imagePath,
        imageToken,
        contentType: "image/jpeg",
        checkPublic: true,
        localBaseUrl: "http://127.0.0.1:43132",
        publicBaseUrl: "https://new-tunnel.example",
        fetcher: async (input) => {
          if (String(input).startsWith("https://")) {
            publicRequests += 1;
            return publicRequests < 3
              ? new Response("temporarily unavailable", { status: 503 })
              : imageResponse();
          }
          return imageResponse();
        },
      },
      3,
      10,
      () => undefined,
      30000,
      async (delayMs) => { delays.push(delayMs); },
    );
    assert.equal(result.validation.valid, true);
    assert.equal(result.retries, 2);
    assert.equal(publicRequests, 3);
    assert.deepEqual(delays, [10, 20]);
  } finally {
    await file.cleanup();
  }
});

test("bounds retries for ngrok 404 failures from an unavailable or outdated public URL", async () => {
  const file = await fixture();
  let publicRequests = 0;
  const delays: number[] = [];
  try {
    await assert.rejects(
      validateScheduledImageWithRetries(
        {
          imagePath: file.imagePath,
          imageToken,
          contentType: "image/jpeg",
          checkPublic: true,
          localBaseUrl: "http://127.0.0.1:43133",
          publicBaseUrl: "https://stale-tunnel.example",
          fetcher: async (input) => {
            if (String(input).startsWith("https://")) {
              publicRequests += 1;
              return new Response("<html>ngrok 404</html>", {
                status: 404,
                headers: { "content-type": "text/html" },
              });
            }
            return imageResponse();
          },
        },
        3,
        10,
        () => undefined,
        30000,
        async (delayMs) => { delays.push(delayMs); },
      ),
      /failed after 3 attempt\(s\).*HTTP 404/,
    );
    assert.equal(publicRequests, 3);
    assert.deepEqual(delays, [10, 20]);
  } finally {
    await file.cleanup();
  }
});

test("checks an actual local image route bound to the configured local port", async () => {
  const file = await fixture();
  const requestedPaths: string[] = [];
  const local = await startServer((server) => {
    server.on("request", (request, response) => {
      requestedPaths.push(request.url ?? "");
      response.writeHead(200, { "content-type": "image/jpeg" });
      response.end(jpegBytes);
    });
  });
  try {
    const validation = await validateScheduledImage({
      imagePath: file.imagePath,
      imageToken,
      contentType: "image/jpeg",
      checkPublic: false,
      localBaseUrl: local.baseUrl,
    });
    assert.equal(validation.valid, true);
    assert.deepEqual(requestedPaths, [`/scheduled-media/${imageToken}`]);
  } finally {
    await local.close();
    await file.cleanup();
  }
});

import assert from "node:assert/strict";
import { readFile } from "node:fs/promises";
import test from "node:test";

process.env["SUPABASE_URL"] = "https://example-project.supabase.co";
process.env["SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY"] = "test-service-role-key";
process.env["SCHEDULE_IMAGE_TIMEOUT_MS"] = "1000";
process.env["SCHEDULE_IMAGE_MAX_BYTES"] = "1024";
process.env["SCHEDULE_VIDEO_MAX_BYTES"] = "1048576";
process.env["SCHEDULE_IMAGE_RETRY_BASE_DELAY_MS"] = "0";
process.env["SCHEDULE_IMAGE_RETRY_MAX_DELAY_MS"] = "0";
process.env["SCHEDULE_SIGNED_URL_TTL_SECONDS"] = "86400";
const storage = await import("../src/storage/scheduled-images.js");
const scheduler = await import("../src/scheduler.js");

const png = Buffer.from([0x89, 0x50, 0x4e, 0x47, 0x0d, 0x0a, 0x1a, 0x0a, 0x00]);
const ownerObject = (owner: string, extension = ".png") =>
  `scheduled/${owner}/${"a".repeat(48)}${extension}`;

async function withFetch(
  mock: (input: RequestInfo | URL, init?: RequestInit) => Promise<Response>,
  run: () => Promise<void>,
): Promise<void> {
  const original = globalThis.fetch;
  globalThis.fetch = mock as typeof fetch;
  try {
    await run();
  } finally {
    globalThis.fetch = original;
  }
}

test("schedules 24 hours and several days ahead, because media is a permanent path", () => {
  const now = Date.UTC(2026, 0, 1, 12, 0, 0);
  const in24Hours = new Date(now + 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000).toISOString();
  const inSevenDays = new Date(now + 7 * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000).toISOString();

  assert.doesNotThrow(() => scheduler.assertFutureScheduleTime(in24Hours, now));
  assert.doesNotThrow(() => scheduler.assertFutureScheduleTime(inSevenDays, now));
  assert.throws(() => scheduler.assertFutureScheduleTime(new Date(now - 1000).toISOString(), now), /future/);
  assert.throws(() => scheduler.assertFutureScheduleTime("not-a-date", now), /future/);
});

test("storage objects are namespaced by user and the segment is always path-safe", () => {
  assert.equal(storage.storageOwnerSegment("alice"), "alice");
  assert.match(storage.storageOwnerSegment("user/../../etc"), /^[a-f0-9]{32}$/);
  assert.match(storage.storageOwnerSegment(""), /^[a-f0-9]{32}$/);

  const owned = ownerObject("alice");
  assert.equal(storage.isOwnedStorageObjectPath(owned, "alice"), true);
  assert.equal(storage.isOwnedStorageObjectPath(owned, "bob"), false);
  assert.throws(() => storage.assertOwnedStorageObjectPath(owned, "bob"), /does not belong to this account/);
});

test("an expiring signed URL can never become the durable media reference", () => {
  const expiredSignedUrl = "https://example-project.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/sign/social-media-images/scheduled/alice/x.png?token=expired";
  assert.equal(storage.isOwnedStorageObjectPath(expiredSignedUrl, "alice"), false);
  assert.throws(() => storage.assertOwnedStorageObjectPath(expiredSignedUrl, "alice"), /does not belong/);

  // Traversal and absolute paths are rejected even with a matching prefix.
  assert.equal(storage.isOwnedStorageObjectPath("scheduled/alice/../bob/x.png", "alice"), false);
  assert.equal(storage.isOwnedStorageObjectPath("/scheduled/alice/" + "a".repeat(48) + ".png", "alice"), false);
});

test("a job scheduled days earlier retrieves the same object and signs a fresh URL at publish time", async () => {
  const objectPath = ownerObject("alice");
  const requests: Array<{ url: string; method?: string; body?: unknown }> = [];

  await withFetch(async (input, init) => {
    requests.push({ url: String(input), method: init?.method, body: init?.body });
    if (init?.method === "POST") {
      // A brand-new signed URL is created now, not at scheduling time.
      return Response.json({ signedURL: `/storage/v1/object/sign/social-media-images/${objectPath}?token=fresh` });
    }
    return new Response(png, {
      status: 200,
      headers: { "content-type": "image/png", "content-length": String(png.length) },
    });
  }, async () => {
    const image = await storage.downloadScheduledImage(objectPath);
    assert.equal(image.contentType, "image/png");
    assert.equal(image.bytes.length, png.length);

    // The download used the permanent private object path with server-side
    // credentials; it never carried an expired URL token.
    const download = requests[0]!;
    assert.equal(download.url, `https://example-project.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/social-media-images/${objectPath}`);
    assert.ok(!download.url.includes("token="));

    const url = await storage.createScheduledImageUrl(objectPath);
    assert.match(url, /\?token=fresh$/);
    assert.deepEqual(JSON.parse(String(requests[1]?.body)), { expiresIn: 86400 });
  });
});

test("publish and retry resolve the same permanent storage path", async () => {
  const source = await readFile(new URL("../src/scheduler.ts", import.meta.url), "utf8");

  // The worker downloads the stored object (server-side credentials) and only
  // creates a signed URL at publish time, for platforms that need one.
  assert.match(source, /downloadScheduledImage\(job\.imageStoragePath\)/);
  assert.match(source, /createScheduledImageUrl\(job\.imageStoragePath\)/);
  assert.match(source, /downloadScheduledVideo\(videoItem\.storagePath\)/);
  assert.match(source, /downloadScheduledDocument\(job\.documentStoragePath\)/);

  // Caller-supplied references are ownership-checked before use.
  assert.match(source, /assertOwnedStorageObjectPath\(imageInput\.storagePath, ownerId\)/);
  assert.match(source, /assertOwnedStorageObjectPath\(item\.storagePath, ownerId\)/);
  assert.match(source, /assertOwnedStorageObjectPath\(document\.storagePath, ownerId\)/);

  // New uploads are namespaced by the authenticated owner.
  assert.match(source, /uploadScheduledImage\(imageBytes, contentType, extension, ownerId\)/);
  assert.match(source, /uploadScheduledVideo\(bytes, item\.contentType, item\.extension\.toLowerCase\(\), ownerId\)/);
  assert.match(source, /uploadScheduledDocument\(documentBytes, documentContentType, "\.pdf", ownerId\)/);

  // The durable reference stored in PostgreSQL is the object path, never a URL.
  assert.match(source, /image_storage_path, content_type/);
  assert.match(source, /storage_path, content_type, created_at/);

  // Retrying reuses the existing row/media and must not clear the reference.
  const retryStart = source.indexOf("export async function retryScheduledPost");
  const retryEnd = source.indexOf("export async function cancelScheduledPost");
  assert.ok(retryStart >= 0 && retryEnd > retryStart);
  const retrySource = source.slice(retryStart, retryEnd);
  assert.doesNotMatch(retrySource, /image_storage_path\s*=\s*NULL|storage_path\s*=\s*NULL/i);
  assert.match(retrySource, /SET status = 'scheduled'/);
});

test("upload API returns the permanent path and scopes the object to the signed-in user", async () => {
  const route = await readFile(
    new URL("../../social-media-web/src/app/api/media/upload/route.ts", import.meta.url),
    "utf8",
  );

  assert.match(route, /const session = await requireApiSession\(\)/);
  assert.match(route, /session\.user\.id/);
  assert.match(route, /uploadScheduledVideo/);
  assert.match(route, /storagePath,/);
  assert.match(route, /expiresInSeconds/);
  assert.doesNotMatch(route, /NEXT_PUBLIC_.*SUPABASE/);
});

]);

async function withFetch(
  mock: (input: RequestInfo | URL, init?: RequestInit) => Promise<Response>,
  run: () => Promise<void>,
): Promise<void> {
  const original = globalThis.fetch;
  globalThis.fetch = mock as typeof fetch;
  try {
    await run();
  } finally {
    globalThis.fetch = original;
  }
}

    assert.match(String(input), /^https:\/\/example-project\.supabase\.co\/storage\/v1\/object\/social-media-images\/scheduled\/user-1\/.+\.mp4$/);
    assert.equal((init?.headers as Record<string, string>)["content-type"], "video/mp4");
    return new Response(null, { status: 200 });
  }, async () => {
    const objectPath = await storage.uploadScheduledVideo(mp4, "video/mp4", ".mp4", "user-1");
    assert.match(objectPath, /^scheduled\/user-1\/[a-f0-9]{48}\.mp4$/);
  });

  await assert.rejects(storage.uploadScheduledVideo(Buffer.from("<html>"), "video/mp4", ".mp4", "user-1"), /does not match video\/mp4/);
  await assert.rejects(storage.uploadScheduledVideo(mp4, "image/png", ".png", "user-1"), /Unsupported scheduled video MIME type/);
});

test("cloud video validation reads the private object and validates the public signed URL", async () => {
  let requestNumber = 0;
  await withFetch(async (_input, init) => {
    requestNumber += 1;
    if (requestNumber === 1) {
      return new Response(mp4, { status: 200, headers: { "content-type": "video/mp4", "content-length": String(mp4.length) } });
    }
    if (requestNumber === 2) {
      assert.equal(init?.method, "POST");
      return Response.json({ signedURL: "https://example-project.supabase.co/signed-video" });
    }
    return new Response(mp4, { status: 200, headers: { "content-type": "video/mp4", "content-length": String(mp4.length) } });
  }, async () => {
    const result = await storage.validateStoredVideo("scheduled/clip.mp4", true);
    assert.equal(result.valid, true);
    assert.equal(result.local.bytes, mp4.length);
    assert.equal(result.public?.valid, true);
    assert.equal(requestNumber, 3);
  });
});

import assert from "node:assert/strict";
import { readFile } from "node:fs/promises";
import test from "node:test";
import {
  canRescheduleScheduledPost,
  normalizeRescheduledTime,
} from "../src/scheduler.js";

test("only posts still waiting to publish can be rescheduled", () => {
  assert.equal(canRescheduleScheduledPost("scheduled"), true);
  assert.equal(canRescheduleScheduledPost("publishing"), false);
  assert.equal(canRescheduleScheduledPost("published"), false);
  assert.equal(canRescheduleScheduledPost("failed"), false);
  assert.equal(canRescheduleScheduledPost("cancelled"), false);
});

test("reschedule validation requires a valid future timestamp", () => {
  const now = Date.UTC(2026, 0, 1, 12, 0, 0);
  const future = new Date(now + 3_600_000).toISOString();
  assert.equal(normalizeRescheduledTime(future, now), future);

  assert.throws(() => normalizeRescheduledTime("", now), /valid date and time/i);
  assert.throws(() => normalizeRescheduledTime("not-a-date", now), /valid date and time/i);
  assert.throws(() => normalizeRescheduledTime(new Date(now).toISOString(), now), /future/i);
  assert.throws(
    () => normalizeRescheduledTime(new Date(now - 60_000).toISOString(), now),
    /future/i,
  );
});

test("rescheduling updates the existing job in place and never inserts a duplicate", async () => {
  const scheduler = await readFile(new URL("../src/scheduler.ts", import.meta.url), "utf8");
  const start = scheduler.indexOf("export async function rescheduleScheduledPost");
  assert.ok(start >= 0, "rescheduleScheduledPost should be exported from the scheduler");
  const source = scheduler.slice(start);

  assert.match(source, /SELECT \* FROM public\.scheduled_posts WHERE id = \$1 AND user_id = \$2 FOR UPDATE/);
  assert.match(source, /UPDATE public\.scheduled_posts\s+SET status = 'scheduled', scheduled_at = \$3/);
  assert.match(source, /claimed_at = NULL/);
  assert.match(source, /canRescheduleScheduledPost\(row\.status\)/);
  assert.doesNotMatch(source, /\bINSERT INTO\b/i);
  assert.doesNotMatch(source, /\bDELETE FROM\b/i);
});

test("the worker claim and the reschedule lock cooperate", async () => {
  const scheduler = await readFile(new URL("../src/scheduler.ts", import.meta.url), "utf8");

  // Resume uses a row lock; the due-job claim skips locked rows so a post being
  // rescheduled is never published at its previous time.
  assert.match(scheduler, /WHERE status = 'scheduled' AND scheduled_at <= NOW\(\)/);
  assert.match(scheduler, /FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED/);
});

  assert.equal(canRescheduleScheduledPost("held"), true);

  assert.equal(canCancelScheduledPost("held"), true);
  assert.equal(canCancelScheduledPost("publishing"), false);
  assert.equal(canCancelScheduledPost("published"), false);

  assert.match(migration, /VALIDATE CONSTRAINT scheduled_posts_status_check/i);

test("the worker claim refuses posts owned by suspended or deleted accounts", async () => {
  const scheduler = await readFile(new URL("../src/scheduler.ts", import.meta.url), "utf8");

  // The original claim guarantees are untouched.
  assert.match(scheduler, /WHERE status = 'scheduled' AND scheduled_at <= NOW\(\)/);

test("holding locks pending rows so racing claims cannot start publishing", async () => {
  const scheduler = await readFile(new URL("../src/scheduler.ts", import.meta.url), "utf8");
  const start = scheduler.indexOf("export async function holdScheduledPostsForUser");
  assert.ok(start >= 0, "holdScheduledPostsForUser should be exported from the scheduler");
  const source = scheduler.slice(start, scheduler.indexOf("export interface ResumeScheduledPostsResult"));

  assert.match(source, /WHERE user_id = \$1 AND status = 'scheduled'\s*\n\s*ORDER BY scheduled_at\s*\n\s*FOR UPDATE/);
  assert.match(source, /SET status = 'held', error = \$2, claimed_at = NULL, updated_at = NOW\(\)/);
  // Holds never delete posts, media, or history.
  assert.doesNotMatch(source, /\bDELETE FROM\b/i);
  assert.doesNotMatch(source, /\bUPDATE public\.scheduled_posts\s+SET scheduled_at\b/i);
});

test("resume re-enables future posts without stale-time republishing of overdue ones", async () => {
  const scheduler = await readFile(new URL("../src/scheduler.ts", import.meta.url), "utf8");
  const start = scheduler.indexOf("export async function resumeScheduledPostsForUser");
  assert.ok(start >= 0, "resumeScheduledPostsForUser should be exported from the scheduler");
  const source = scheduler.slice(start);

  assert.match(source, /SELECT \* FROM public\.scheduled_posts\s*\n\s*WHERE user_id = \$1 AND status = 'held' AND \(\$2::text IS NULL OR id = \$2\)\s*\n\s*ORDER BY scheduled_at\s*\n\s*FOR UPDATE/);
  assert.match(source, /const overdue = row\.scheduled_at\.getTime\(\) <= Date\.now\(\)/);
  assert.match(source, /Still held: the original schedule time has passed\. Reschedule the post explicitly\./);
  assert.match(source, /SET status = 'scheduled', error = NULL, claimed_at = NULL/);
  // Resume never publishes at a stale time and never duplicates posts: no
  // scheduled_at rewrite for resumed rows and no new rows at all.
  assert.doesNotMatch(source, /SET scheduled_at =/);
  assert.doesNotMatch(source, /\bINSERT INTO public\.scheduled_posts\b/i);
});

import assert from "node:assert/strict";
import { readFile } from "node:fs/promises";
import test from "node:test";

const { dedupeStorageCandidates } = await import("../src/scheduler.js");

// --- Pure helper -------------------------------------------------------------

test("storage cleanup candidates are deduplicated by path keeping the first kind", () => {
  const deduped = dedupeStorageCandidates([
    { kind: "image", path: "scheduled/owner/aaa.jpg" },
    { kind: "video", path: "scheduled/owner/bbb.mp4" },
    { kind: "image", path: "scheduled/owner/aaa.jpg" },
    { kind: "image", path: "" },
  ]);
  assert.deepEqual(deduped, [
    { kind: "image", path: "scheduled/owner/aaa.jpg" },
    { kind: "video", path: "scheduled/owner/bbb.mp4" },
  ]);
});

// --- Reference-counted deletion (source assertions per project convention) ---

test("cleanup helper counts references in posts and media tables, honoring active statuses", async () => {
  const scheduler = await readFile(new URL("../src/scheduler.ts", import.meta.url), "utf8");
  assert.match(scheduler, /post\.image_storage_path = ANY\(\$1::text\[\]\)/);
  assert.match(scheduler, /post\.document_storage_path = ANY\(\$1::text\[\]\)/);
  assert.match(scheduler, /media_ref\.storage_path = ANY\(\$1::text\[\]\)/);
  assert.match(scheduler, /JOIN public\.scheduled_posts AS post ON post\.id = media_ref\.post_id/);
  assert.match(scheduler, /refs\.status IN \('scheduled', 'publishing', 'held'\)/, "held posts keep their shared media references live for resume");
});

test("cleanup helper is concurrency-safe and fails safe", async () => {
  const scheduler = await readFile(new URL("../src/scheduler.ts", import.meta.url), "utf8");
  const helper = scheduler.slice(
    scheduler.indexOf("async function deleteUnreferencedStorageObjects"),
    scheduler.indexOf("export async function cancelScheduledPost"),
  );
  assert.match(helper, /BEGIN/);
  assert.match(helper, /COMMIT/);
  assert.match(helper, /pg_advisory_xact_lock/, "per-path advisory locks serialize racing cleanups");
  assert.match(helper, /sort\(\(a, b\) => a\.path\.localeCompare\(b\.path\)\)/, "sorted lock order prevents deadlocks");
  assert.match(helper, /scheduled_shared_object_cleanup_skipped/, "unverifiable references must not delete");
  assert.match(helper, /deleted\.add\(candidate\.path\)/, "per-path outcomes are reported to callers");
  assert.match(helper, /HTTP 404/, "an object Supabase reports as missing still counts as cleaned up");
  const referenceIndex = helper.indexOf("const referenced = new Set");
  const deleteIndex = helper.indexOf("deleteScheduledVideo");
  const beginIndex = helper.indexOf('"BEGIN"');
  assert.ok(beginIndex >= 0 && referenceIndex > beginIndex && deleteIndex > referenceIndex, "deletes happen after the reference count");
});

test("cancel routes shared objects through the reference-counted helper", async () => {
  const scheduler = await readFile(new URL("../src/scheduler.ts", import.meta.url), "utf8");
  const cancel = scheduler.slice(
    scheduler.indexOf("export async function cancelScheduledPost"),
    scheduler.indexOf("export async function rescheduleScheduledPost"),
  );
  assert.match(cancel, /deleteUnreferencedStorageObjects\(storageObjects\)/);
  assert.doesNotMatch(cancel, /deleteScheduled(Video|Image|Document)\(/, "cancel must never delete unconditionally");
  assert.match(cancel, /unregisterScheduledMedia/, "media token registration is still cleaned up");
  assert.match(cancel, /await unlink\(file\)/, "local files remain directly deleted (never shared)");
  assert.match(cancel, /kind: "document", path: row\.document_storage_path/, "documents join the reference check");
  assert.match(cancel, /WHERE id = \$1 AND user_id = \$2 AND status IN \('scheduled', 'held'\)/, "cancel still only applies to unclaimed posts (scheduled or held, never publishing/published)");
});

test("scheduling failure cleanup no longer deletes shared references unconditionally", async () => {
  const scheduler = await readFile(new URL("../src/scheduler.ts", import.meta.url), "utf8");
  assert.doesNotMatch(scheduler, /deleteScheduledImage\(imageStoragePath\)/);
  assert.doesNotMatch(scheduler, /deleteScheduledDocument\(documentFields\.documentStoragePath\)/);
  const mediaCatch = scheduler.slice(
    scheduler.indexOf("const cleanupCandidates: StorageObjectCandidate[] = ["),
    scheduler.indexOf("throw error;\n  }\n}", scheduler.indexOf("const cleanupCandidates: StorageObjectCandidate[] = [")),
  );
  assert.match(mediaCatch, /deleteUnreferencedStorageObjects\(cleanupCandidates\)/);
  assert.match(scheduler, /Reference-counted cleanup: the row inserts rolled back/);
});

test("publishing still retrieves shared media through the stored permanent paths", async () => {
  const scheduler = await readFile(new URL("../src/scheduler.ts", import.meta.url), "utf8");
  assert.match(scheduler, /await downloadScheduledImage\(job\.imageStoragePath\)/, "LinkedIn publish download");
  assert.match(scheduler, /await downloadScheduledVideo\(videoItem\.storagePath\)/, "video publish download");
  assert.match(scheduler, /await createScheduledImageUrl\(job\.imageStoragePath\)/, "Meta publish fresh signed URL");
  assert.match(scheduler, /await downloadScheduledDocument\(job\.documentStoragePath\)/, "document publish download");
  assert.doesNotMatch(scheduler, /deleteScheduled.*publishing/, "no publish path deletes storage objects");
});

test("ownership validation and legacy flat paths are preserved", async () => {
  const storage = await readFile(new URL("../src/storage/scheduled-images.ts", import.meta.url), "utf8");
  assert.match(storage, /export function storageOwnerSegment/);
  assert.match(storage, /export function isOwnedStorageObjectPath/);
  assert.match(storage, /export function assertOwnedStorageObjectPath/);
  const scheduler = await readFile(new URL("../src/scheduler.ts", import.meta.url), "utf8");
  assert.match(scheduler, /assertOwnedStorageObjectPath\(imageInput\.storagePath, ownerId\)/, "scheduling input validation unchanged");
  assert.match(scheduler, /assertOwnedStorageObjectPath\(item\.storagePath, ownerId\)/, "media input validation unchanged");
  const helper = scheduler.slice(

  );

  assert.doesNotMatch(helper, /isOwnedStorageObjectPath|storageFilePattern/);
});

FILE: social-media-mcp/tests/validation.test.ts

import assert from "node:assert/strict";
import test from "node:test";
import {
  platformImageRequirements,
  validateImageUrl,
  validateLinkedInAuthorUrn,
  validatePostContent,
} from "../src/utils/validation.js";

test("requires publicly fetchable HTTPS media URLs", () => {
  assert.equal(validateImageUrl("https://cdn.example.com/image.jpg"), undefined);
  assert.match(validateImageUrl("http://cdn.example.com/image.jpg") ?? "", /HTTPS/);
  assert.match(validateImageUrl("not-a-url") ?? "", /absolute URL/);
});

test("remote image inputs accept only validated HTTPS URLs", () => {
  for (const url of ["https://cdn.example.com/a.png", "https://8.8.8.8/a.jpg"]) {
    assert.equal(validateImageUrl(url), undefined, `${url} should be accepted`);
  }
  for (const url of ["http://cdn.example.com/a.png", "ftp://cdn.example.com/a.png", "file:///etc/passwd"]) {
    assert.match(validateImageUrl(url) ?? "", /HTTPS/, `${url} should be rejected`);
  }
});

test("validates LinkedIn author URNs", () => {
  assert.equal(validateLinkedInAuthorUrn("urn:li:person:abc_123"), undefined);
  assert.equal(validateLinkedInAuthorUrn("urn:li:organization:12345"), undefined);
  assert.match(validateLinkedInAuthorUrn("urn:li:share:123") ?? "", /author/);
});

test("enforces platform image requirements and accepts non-empty text", () => {
  assert.deepEqual(platformImageRequirements("instagram"), [
    "Instagram Graph API feed publishing requires an image reference; text-only posts are not supported.",
  ]);
  assert.deepEqual(platformImageRequirements("linkedin", "https://example.com/a.jpg"), []);
  assert.deepEqual(platformImageRequirements("linkedin", "https://example.com/a.jpg", "C:\\a.jpg"), [
    "LinkedIn uses either imagePath or imageUrl, not both.",
  ]);
  assert.deepEqual(validatePostContent("A test caption"), []);
  assert.deepEqual(validatePostContent(), [
    "Provide post text, an image URL, an image path, or an imageStoragePath.",
  ]);
});

test("permanent storage object paths satisfy platform image requirements exclusively", () => {
  assert.deepEqual(platformImageRequirements("instagram", undefined, undefined, "scheduled/owner/a.jpg"), []);
  assert.deepEqual(platformImageRequirements("facebook", undefined, undefined, "scheduled/owner/a.jpg"), []);
  assert.deepEqual(platformImageRequirements("linkedin", undefined, undefined, "scheduled/owner/a.jpg"), []);
  assert.deepEqual(platformImageRequirements("instagram", "https://example.com/a.jpg", undefined, "scheduled/owner/a.jpg"), [
    "Provide only one image reference: imageUrl, imagePath, or imageStoragePath.",
  ]);
  assert.deepEqual(platformImageRequirements("facebook", undefined, "C:\\a.jpg", "scheduled/owner/a.jpg"), [
    "Provide only one image reference: imageUrl, imagePath, or imageStoragePath.",
    "Meta publishing uses imageUrl or a storage object path; local image uploads are not implemented for this platform.",
  ]);
  assert.deepEqual(validatePostContent(undefined, undefined, undefined, "scheduled/owner/a.jpg"), []);
});

# Reuse the backend PostgreSQL connection (also read from ../social-media-mcp/.env).
# Serverless hosts (Vercel) MUST use the Supabase connection pooler (transaction
# mode, port 6543) so many isolates share a small number of database
# connections; direct connections (db.<ref>.supabase.co:5432) can exhaust the
# provider's connection cap and intermittently fail session verification. Keep
# the direct URL only for long-running workers (Render).
# Pooler (Vercel):   postgresql://postgres.<ref>:PASSWORD@aws-0-<region>.pooler.supabase.com:6543/postgres?sslmode=require
# Direct (Render):   postgresql://postgres:PASSWORD@db.<ref>.supabase.co:5432/postgres?sslmode=require
# When the URL has no sslmode parameter, the app still enforces TLS for
# *.supabase.co hosts automatically.
# DATABASE_URL=

# Generate with: node -e "console.log(require('node:crypto').randomBytes(32).toString('hex'))"
BETTER_AUTH_SECRET=
BETTER_AUTH_URL=http://localhost:3000
NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL=http://localhost:3000

# Used only by scripts/seed-admin.ts to provision the single admin account.
ADMIN_EMAIL=
ADMIN_PASSWORD=
ADMIN_NAME=Administrator

# Public sign-up is enabled by default. Set to false to restrict account creation to scripts/seed-admin.ts.
ALLOW_ADMIN_SIGNUP=true

# --- Security email delivery (OTP password recovery) ---
# Password recovery emails a 6-digit, single-use code that expires in 5 minutes.
# Configure ONE transport. Never put these values in NEXT_PUBLIC_* or the client.
# Resend (recommended):
# RESEND_API_KEY=
# EMAIL_FROM="Social Console <security@your-domain.example>"
# EMAIL_APP_NAME=Social Console
# ...or a generic HTTPS webhook that accepts { to, subject, text }:
# EMAIL_DELIVERY_URL=
# EMAIL_DELIVERY_TOKEN=

# --- Emergency Super Admin recovery (offline CLI only) ---
# There is no HTTP endpoint for this. Run: npm run db:recover-admin
# The acknowledgement phrase is required so an accidental run cannot rotate the
# administrator password or revoke sessions.
# RECOVER_ADMIN_ACKNOWLEDGE=recover-super-admin
# ADMIN_NEW_PASSWORD=

# --- Backend OAuth configuration (read by the compiled social-media-mcp modules) ---
# The frontend imports the backend from ../social-media-mcp/dist, so these must be
# present in the Vercel environment. Set OAUTH_CALLBACK_MODE=cloud for production.
# Only public client IDs are needed here; never put Meta/Instagram/LinkedIn client
# secrets or CLOUD_TOKEN_ENCRYPTION_KEY on Vercel.
# OAUTH_CALLBACK_MODE=cloud
# OAUTH_REDIRECT_BASE_URL=https://social-media-cloud-worker.onrender.com
# OAUTH_FRONTEND_BASE_URL=https://YOUR-VERCEL-PROJECT.vercel.app
# META_APP_ID=
# INSTAGRAM_APP_ID=
# LINKEDIN_CLIENT_ID=

# --- Remote MCP consent (Render authorization server) ---
# The Vercel app renders the consent screen and creates the one-time code, so it
# must validate the same MCP resource, scope, and redirect-origin allowlist as the
# Render worker. These values are public and must match Render exactly.
# MCP_PUBLIC_URL=https://social-media-cloud-worker.onrender.com/mcp
# MCP_OAUTH_SCOPE=mcp
# MCP_ALLOWED_REDIRECT_ORIGINS=https://claude.ai,https://claude.com
# MCP_ALLOW_LOOPBACK_REDIRECTS=true

# Required on Vercel: POST /api/credentials encrypts each user's Developer App
# secret before it is stored in PostgreSQL. This MUST be the same 32-byte key as
# the Render worker (which decrypts during the OAuth exchange and LinkedIn
# refresh). Generate with:
#   node -e "console.log(require('node:crypto').randomBytes(32).toString('hex'))"
# Never expose it through NEXT_PUBLIC_*, a client bundle, an API response, or logs.
# APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY=

# --- Remote media upload (POST /api/media/upload) ---
# Required when signed-in users need to turn a local image, video, or PDF into a
# durable media reference for remote MCP tools (Claude.ai cannot attach files to
# a remote tool). The endpoint stores the file under a per-user prefix in the
# private `social-media-images` bucket and returns the permanent object path
# (`storagePath`); scheduling tools persist that path and the worker re-downloads
# it at publish time. Server-side only: never expose SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY
# through NEXT_PUBLIC_*, a client bundle, an API response, or logs. The bucket
# must stay private.
# SUPABASE_URL=
# SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY=

# Lifetime in seconds of the signed URL the worker creates at publish time (not
# stored; regenerated for every attempt). Default 86400, max 604800. Only needs
# to outlive the destination platform's fetch of the media.
# SCHEDULE_SIGNED_URL_TTL_SECONDS=86400

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS "user" (
  "id" text PRIMARY KEY NOT NULL,
  "name" text NOT NULL,
  "email" text NOT NULL UNIQUE,
  "email_verified" boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT false,
  "image" text,
  "created_at" timestamp with time zone NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  "updated_at" timestamp with time zone NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS "session" (
  "id" text PRIMARY KEY NOT NULL,
  "expires_at" timestamp with time zone NOT NULL,
  "token" text NOT NULL UNIQUE,
  "created_at" timestamp with time zone NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  "updated_at" timestamp with time zone NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  "ip_address" text,
  "user_agent" text,
  "user_id" text NOT NULL REFERENCES "user" ("id") ON DELETE CASCADE
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS "account" (
  "id" text PRIMARY KEY NOT NULL,
  "account_id" text NOT NULL,
  "provider_id" text NOT NULL,
  "user_id" text NOT NULL REFERENCES "user" ("id") ON DELETE CASCADE,
  "access_token" text,
  "refresh_token" text,
  "id_token" text,
  "access_token_expires_at" timestamp with time zone,
  "refresh_token_expires_at" timestamp with time zone,
  "scope" text,
  "password" text,
  "created_at" timestamp with time zone NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  "updated_at" timestamp with time zone NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS "verification" (
  "id" text PRIMARY KEY NOT NULL,
  "identifier" text NOT NULL,
  "value" text NOT NULL,
  "expires_at" timestamp with time zone NOT NULL,
  "created_at" timestamp with time zone DEFAULT now(),
  "updated_at" timestamp with time zone DEFAULT now()
);

CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS "session_user_id_idx" ON "session" ("user_id");
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS "account_user_id_idx" ON "account" ("user_id");
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS "verification_identifier_idx" ON "verification" ("identifier");

FILE: social-media-web/migrations/0002_admin_multitenant.sql

-- 0002_admin_multitenant.sql
--
-- Single Super Admin + multi-user management foundation (Phase 2).
--
-- Extends the Better Auth user table in place; nothing existing is dropped or
-- reset. Complements Better Auth 1.7.9's admin plugin, which supplies the
-- `role`, `banned`, `ban_reason`, and `ban_expires` columns.
--
-- approval_status semantics:
--   pending  - registration awaiting admin approval (default for NEW users)
--   approved - full access
--   rejected - registration denied
--   suspended / deleted are expressed through the admin plugin's `banned`
--   flag and the `deleted_at` column respectively (no duplicate mechanism).
--
-- Existing users are explicitly marked approved so no production account
-- loses access when this migration runs. The default is set to 'pending'
-- afterwards so every newly created user starts unapproved.

ALTER TABLE "user" ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS "role" text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'user';
ALTER TABLE "user" ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS "banned" boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT false;
ALTER TABLE "user" ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS "ban_reason" text;
ALTER TABLE "user" ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS "ban_expires" timestamp with time zone;

-- 1. Add without affecting existing rows, 2. mark every existing user
-- approved, 3. switch the default so new signups start pending.
ALTER TABLE "user" ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS "approval_status" text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'approved';
UPDATE "user" SET "approval_status" = 'approved' WHERE "approval_status" IS NULL;
ALTER TABLE "user" ALTER COLUMN "approval_status" DROP DEFAULT;
ALTER TABLE "user" ALTER COLUMN "approval_status" SET DEFAULT 'pending';

ALTER TABLE "user" ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS "deleted_at" timestamp with time zone;

DO $$
BEGIN
  IF NOT EXISTS (
    SELECT 1 FROM pg_constraint WHERE conname = 'user_role_check'
  ) THEN
    ALTER TABLE "user"
      ADD CONSTRAINT user_role_check CHECK (role IN ('admin', 'user')) NOT VALID;
  END IF;

  IF NOT EXISTS (
    SELECT 1 FROM pg_constraint WHERE conname = 'user_approval_status_check'
  ) THEN
    ALTER TABLE "user"
      ADD CONSTRAINT user_approval_status_check
      CHECK (approval_status IN ('pending', 'approved', 'rejected')) NOT VALID;
  END IF;
END
$$;

ALTER TABLE "user"
  VALIDATE CONSTRAINT user_role_check,
  VALIDATE CONSTRAINT user_approval_status_check;

CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS "user_approval_status_idx" ON "user" ("approval_status");

-- Database-level single-Super-Admin invariant: the partial unique index makes
-- a second row with role='admin' impossible even under concurrent seeds or a
-- manipulated admin API call, independently of any application logic.
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS "user_single_admin_idx"
  ON "user" ("role")
  WHERE "role" = 'admin';

-- Activity / audit log. DDL mirrors social-media-mcp/migrations/013_account_hold.sql
-- so both packages converge on the same table regardless of which migration
-- runs first (both are idempotent). Writers must never store passwords,
-- tokens, secrets, or encryption keys in metadata.
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS "activity_log" (
  "id" text PRIMARY KEY,
  "actor_user_id" text,
  "target_user_id" text,
  "action" text NOT NULL CHECK ("action" <> ''),
  "resource_type" text NOT NULL CHECK ("resource_type" <> ''),
  "resource_id" text,
  "metadata" jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}'::jsonb,
  "created_at" timestamp with time zone NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);

CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS "activity_log_created_at_idx" ON "activity_log" ("created_at" DESC);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS "activity_log_target_user_idx" ON "activity_log" ("target_user_id", "created_at" DESC);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS "activity_log_actor_user_idx" ON "activity_log" ("actor_user_id", "created_at" DESC);

ALTER TABLE "activity_log" ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;
REVOKE ALL ON TABLE "activity_log" FROM PUBLIC, anon, authenticated;
GRANT ALL ON TABLE "activity_log" TO service_role;

FILE: social-media-web/migrations/0003_admin_rls.sql
================================================================================

-- 0003_admin_rls.sql
--
-- Additive row-level-security audit hardening for Phase 3.
--
-- IMPORTANT
-- ---------
-- This file is NOT part of the MCP auto-migration list and is NOT applied by
-- `npm run db:migrate` unless an operator explicitly points the migration
-- runner at it. Review the application's database role before running it.
--
-- What it does:
--   1. Enables RLS on the scheduler table and the Better Auth tables that did
--      not previously have it (`scheduled_posts`, `user`, `session`, `account`,
--      `verification`).
--   2. Revokes access from PUBLIC and (when present) Supabase's `anon` and
--      `authenticated` roles, so browser-facing PostgREST access cannot read or
--      mutate these tables directly.
--   3. Grants the server-side `service_role` full access through an explicit
--      permissive policy.
--
-- What it deliberately does NOT do:
--   - It does not force row-level security. The table owner (the role the
--     application normally connects with) continues to bypass RLS exactly as
--     before, so a deployment that connects as the owner is unaffected.
--   - It does not drop, rename, or remove any data.
--   - It does not change existing `activity_log` policies.
--
-- If the application connects as a non-owner role other than `service_role`,
-- grant that role access (and add an explicit policy) before applying this
-- file, or skip it. Enabling RLS without grants would deny that role access.

DO $$
DECLARE
  target_table text;
BEGIN
  FOREACH target_table IN ARRAY ARRAY[
    'scheduled_posts',
    'user',
    'session',
    'account',
    'verification'
  ]
  LOOP
    IF NOT EXISTS (
      SELECT 1
        FROM pg_tables
       WHERE schemaname = 'public'
         AND tablename = target_table
    ) THEN
      CONTINUE;
    END IF;

    -- Enabling RLS without FORCE keeps the owner's bypass behaviour intact.
    EXECUTE format('ALTER TABLE public.%I ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY', target_table);
    EXECUTE format('REVOKE ALL ON TABLE public.%I FROM PUBLIC', target_table);

    IF EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM pg_roles WHERE rolname = 'anon') THEN
      EXECUTE format('REVOKE ALL ON TABLE public.%I FROM anon', target_table);
    END IF;

    IF EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM pg_roles WHERE rolname = 'authenticated') THEN
      EXECUTE format('REVOKE ALL ON TABLE public.%I FROM authenticated', target_table);
    END IF;

    IF EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM pg_roles WHERE rolname = 'service_role') THEN
      EXECUTE format('GRANT ALL ON TABLE public.%I TO service_role', target_table);

      IF NOT EXISTS (
        SELECT 1
          FROM pg_policies
         WHERE schemaname = 'public'
           AND tablename = target_table
           AND policyname = target_table || '_service_role'
      ) THEN
        EXECUTE format(
          'CREATE POLICY %I ON public.%I FOR ALL TO service_role USING (true) WITH CHECK (true)',
          target_table || '_service_role',
          target_table
        );
      END IF;
    END IF;
  END LOOP;
END
$$;

-- Keep the existing audit table locked down; re-assert idempotently in case an
-- earlier deployment skipped the grants.
DO $$
BEGIN
  IF EXISTS (
    SELECT 1
      FROM pg_tables
     WHERE schemaname = 'public'
       AND tablename = 'activity_log'
  ) THEN
    EXECUTE 'ALTER TABLE public.activity_log ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY';
    EXECUTE 'REVOKE ALL ON TABLE public.activity_log FROM PUBLIC';

    IF EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM pg_roles WHERE rolname = 'anon') THEN
      EXECUTE 'REVOKE ALL ON TABLE public.activity_log FROM anon';
    END IF;

    IF EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM pg_roles WHERE rolname = 'authenticated') THEN
      EXECUTE 'REVOKE ALL ON TABLE public.activity_log FROM authenticated';
    END IF;

    IF EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM pg_roles WHERE rolname = 'service_role') THEN
      EXECUTE 'GRANT ALL ON TABLE public.activity_log TO service_role';
    END IF;
  END IF;
END
$$;

-- node_modules/better-auth/dist/plugins/admin/schema.mjs) expects a nullable

-- admin starts impersonation and tells the plugin which admin session owns

-- include it, so it is added here as its own idempotent step.

-- Snake_case column name matches the package's field-naming convention
-- (email_verified, ip_address, ban_reason, ...). The column is nullable so
-- every existing session row keeps its meaning: nobody is impersonating.
-- Nothing is dropped or modified.

FILE: social-media-web/README.md
