import { and, asc, count, desc, eq, ilike, or } from "drizzle-orm";

import { logActivity } from "@/lib/activity";
import { getAdminUserStats } from "@/lib/admin-overview";
import {
  nonAdminCondition,
  userStatusCondition,
} from "@/lib/admin-user-filters";
import {
  classifyUserStatus,
  type UserStatus,
} from "@/lib/admin-user-status";
import { ApiError } from "@/lib/api";
import { db } from "@/lib/db";
import { isUniqueViolation } from "@/lib/db-errors";
import { account, session, user } from "@/lib/db/schema";
import {
  type ApprovalStatus,
  type UserFilters,
  type UserRole,
  type UserUpdate,
  validateUserUpdate,
} from "@/lib/admin-users-policy";

export interface AdminUserSummary {
  id: string;
  name: string;
  email: string;
  role: UserRole;
  status: UserStatus;
  approvalStatus: ApprovalStatus;
  banned: boolean;
  createdAt: string;
  deletedAt: string | null;
}

export interface AdminUserDetail extends AdminUserSummary {
  emailVerified: boolean;
  image: string | null;
  banReason: string | null;
  banExpires: string | null;
  updatedAt: string;
  hasPassword: boolean;
  sessionCount: number;
}

export interface AdminUserCounts {
  total: number;
  pending: number;
  active: number;
  inactive: number;
}

export interface AdminUserList {
  users: AdminUserSummary[];
  counts: AdminUserCounts;
}

interface UserRow {
  id: string;
  name: string;
  email: string;
  role: string;
  approvalStatus: string;
  banned: boolean;
  createdAt: Date;
  updatedAt: Date;
  emailVerified: boolean;
  image: string | null;
  banReason: string | null;
  banExpires: Date | null;
  deletedAt: Date | null;
}

// Escape LIKE metacharacters so a search for "100%" is a literal search.
function escapeLike(value: string): string {
  return value.replace(/[\\%_]/g, (character) => `\\${character}`);
}

function asRole(value: string): UserRole {
  return value === "admin" ? "admin" : "user";
}

function asApprovalStatus(value: string): ApprovalStatus {
  if (value === "approved" || value === "rejected") return value;
  return "pending";
}

function toSummary(row: UserRow): AdminUserSummary {
  return {
    id: row.id,
    name: row.name,
    email: row.email,
    role: asRole(row.role),
    status: classifyUserStatus({
      approvalStatus: row.approvalStatus,
      banned: row.banned,
      deleted: row.deletedAt !== null,
    }),
    approvalStatus: asApprovalStatus(row.approvalStatus),
    banned: row.banned,
    createdAt: row.createdAt.toISOString(),
    deletedAt: row.deletedAt ? row.deletedAt.toISOString() : null,
  };
}

export async function listUsers(filters: UserFilters): Promise<AdminUserList> {
  const conditions = [];
  if (filters.query) {
    const pattern = `%${escapeLike(filters.query)}%`;
    conditions.push(or(ilike(user.name, pattern), ilike(user.email, pattern))!);
  }
  if (filters.status !== "all") {
    conditions.push(userStatusCondition(filters.status));
  }
  if (filters.role !== "all") {
    conditions.push(eq(user.role, filters.role));
  } else {
    // The default directory and the dashboard card links are normal-user
    // views, so they must exclude the Super Admin just like the statistics.
    // Selecting the "Super Admin" role filter still lists that account.
    conditions.push(nonAdminCondition());
  }

  const rows = (await db
    .select({
      id: user.id,
      name: user.name,
      email: user.email,
      role: user.role,
      approvalStatus: user.approvalStatus,
      banned: user.banned,
      createdAt: user.createdAt,
      updatedAt: user.updatedAt,
      emailVerified: user.emailVerified,
      image: user.image,
      banReason: user.banReason,
      banExpires: user.banExpires,
      deletedAt: user.deletedAt,
    })
    .from(user)
    .where(conditions.length > 0 ? and(...conditions) : undefined)
    .orderBy(desc(user.createdAt), asc(user.email))) as UserRow[];

  // Reuse the dashboard aggregate so the cards and the directory can never
  // disagree: total counts every non-admin row, while pending/active/inactive
  // use the same classification rules as the status filters. Both queries stay
  // in PostgreSQL.
  const stats = await getAdminUserStats();

  const counts: AdminUserCounts = {
    total: stats.total,
    pending: stats.pending,
    active: stats.active,
    inactive: stats.inactive,
  };

  return { users: rows.map(toSummary), counts };
}

export async function getUserDetail(id: string): Promise<AdminUserDetail | null> {
  const [row] = (await db
    .select({
      id: user.id,
      name: user.name,
      email: user.email,
      role: user.role,
      approvalStatus: user.approvalStatus,
      banned: user.banned,
      createdAt: user.createdAt,
      updatedAt: user.updatedAt,
      emailVerified: user.emailVerified,
      image: user.image,
      banReason: user.banReason,
      banExpires: user.banExpires,
      deletedAt: user.deletedAt,
    })
    .from(user)
    .where(eq(user.id, id))
    .limit(1)) as UserRow[];

  if (!row) return null;

  const [credential] = await db
    .select({ id: account.id })
    .from(account)
    .where(and(eq(account.userId, id), eq(account.providerId, "credential")))
    .limit(1);

  const [sessionCount] = await db
    .select({ total: count() })
    .from(session)
    .where(eq(session.userId, id));

  return {
    ...toSummary(row),
    emailVerified: row.emailVerified,
    image: row.image,
    banReason: row.banReason,
    banExpires: row.banExpires ? row.banExpires.toISOString() : null,
    updatedAt: row.updatedAt.toISOString(),
    hasPassword: Boolean(credential),
    sessionCount: Number(sessionCount?.total ?? 0),
  };
}

export async function updateUser(
  actorId: string,
  targetId: string,
  update: UserUpdate,
): Promise<AdminUserSummary> {
  try {
    return await db.transaction(async (tx) => {
      const [row] = (await tx
        .select({
          id: user.id,
          name: user.name,
          email: user.email,
          role: user.role,
          approvalStatus: user.approvalStatus,
          banned: user.banned,
          createdAt: user.createdAt,
          updatedAt: user.updatedAt,
          emailVerified: user.emailVerified,
          image: user.image,
          banReason: user.banReason,
          banExpires: user.banExpires,
          deletedAt: user.deletedAt,
        })
        .from(user)
        .where(eq(user.id, targetId))
        .limit(1)) as UserRow[];

      if (!row) throw new ApiError("User not found.", 404);

      const adminRows = await tx
        .select({ id: user.id })
        .from(user)
        .where(eq(user.role, "admin"));

      const violation = validateUserUpdate({
        actorId,
        target: row,
        update,
        adminCount: adminRows.length,
      });
      if (violation) throw new ApiError(violation.message, violation.status);

      const patch: Partial<typeof user.$inferInsert> = { updatedAt: new Date() };
      if (update.role) patch.role = update.role;
      if (update.approvalStatus) patch.approvalStatus = update.approvalStatus;

      await tx.update(user).set(patch).where(eq(user.id, targetId));

      await logActivity(
        {
          actorUserId: actorId,
          targetUserId: targetId,
          action: update.role
            ? "user_role_changed"
            : update.approvalStatus === "approved"
              ? "user_approved"
              : "user_rejected",
          resourceType: "user",
          resourceId: targetId,
          metadata: {
            previousRole: row.role,
            role: update.role ?? row.role,
            previousApprovalStatus: row.approvalStatus,
            approvalStatus: update.approvalStatus ?? row.approvalStatus,
          },
        },
        tx,
      );

      return toSummary({
        ...row,
        role: update.role ?? row.role,
        approvalStatus: update.approvalStatus ?? row.approvalStatus,
        updatedAt: new Date(),
      });
    });
  } catch (error) {
    // Defense in depth: the partial unique index on role='admin' can still fire
    // under a concurrent request even though this transaction checked first.
    if (isUniqueViolation(error)) {
      throw new ApiError(
        "A Super Admin already exists. The application supports exactly one admin account.",
        409,
      );
    }
    throw error;
  }
}

import { headers } from "next/headers";

import { auth } from "@/lib/auth";
import {
  ApprovalRequiredError,
  SessionUnavailableError,
  requireApprovedUser,
  UnauthorizedError,
} from "@/lib/session";

export class ApiError extends Error {
  readonly status: number;

  constructor(message: string, status = 400) {
    super(message);
    this.name = "ApiError";
    this.status = status;
  }
}

// Standard protected-API helper. Beyond session validity it enforces the
// account-approval gate: pending, rejected, suspended, and soft-deleted users
// are rejected even if a previously issued session cookie is still valid.
// Admin-only routes must additionally call requireAdmin() from "@/lib/session".
export async function requireApiSession() {
  return requireApprovedUser();
}

export async function currentSessionOrNull() {
  return auth.api.getSession({ headers: await headers() });
}

export function apiErrorResponse(error: unknown): Response {
  if (error instanceof ApiError) {
    return Response.json({ error: error.message }, { status: error.status });
  }
  if (error instanceof UnauthorizedError) {
    return Response.json({ error: error.message }, { status: 401 });
  }
  if (error instanceof ApprovalRequiredError) {
    return Response.json({ error: error.message, code: error.code }, { status: 403 });
  }
  if (error instanceof SessionUnavailableError) {
    // 503, not 500 or 401: the caller is still authenticated; the session
    // store is temporarily unreachable. Clients may retry.
    return Response.json({ error: error.message, code: error.code }, { status: 503 });
  }
  console.error("[api] unhandled error:", error);
  const message = error instanceof Error ? error.message : "Unexpected error.";
  return Response.json({ error: message }, { status: 500 });
}

  baseURL,
  "https://social-media-mcp-facebook-instagram.vercel.app",
  ...(process.env.NODE_ENV === "development"
    ? ["http://localhost:3000"]
    : []),
];

// Shown to a user whose account was suspended when they try to sign in.
// Contains no account details beyond the plain suspension notice.
const BANNED_USER_MESSAGE =
  "This account has been suspended. Contact the administrator if you believe this is a mistake.";

// The single Super Admin signature used to detect an existing admin row.
export const ADMIN_ROLE = "admin";

// Better Auth wraps every failed database operation in an opaque APIError and
// only passes the real database error to its internal logger. Capture it so
// production logs identify the actual connectivity failure (ECONNRESET, "too
// many clients", ...) instead of the generic "Failed to get session". Values
// are redacted: a database error message can carry bound parameters such as
// the session token, so URLs are stripped and the text truncated.
function redactDatabaseError(text: string): string {
  return text
    .replace(/postgres(?:ql)?:\/\/[^\s"'<>]+/gi, "[database URL redacted]")
    .slice(0, 300);
}

const authLogger = {
  log: (level: "debug" | "info" | "warn" | "error", message: string, ...args: unknown[]) => {
    if (level === "error") {
      const cause = [message, ...args].find((a): a is Error => a instanceof Error);
      if (cause) {
        console.error(
          JSON.stringify({
            event: "better_auth_internal_error",
            name: cause.name,
            code: (cause as NodeJS.ErrnoException).code ?? undefined,
            message: redactDatabaseError(cause.message),
          }),
        );
        return;
      }
    }
    // Preserve Better Auth's default output (its default level is "warn", so
    // only warn/error reach this hook) for every other event.
    const write = level === "error" ? console.error : console.warn;
    write(`[Better Auth]: ${message}`, ...args.filter((a) => typeof a === "string"));
  },
};

export const auth = betterAuth({
  database: drizzleAdapter(db, { provider: "pg", schema }),
  secret: process.env.BETTER_AUTH_SECRET,
  baseURL,
  logger: authLogger,
  trustedOrigins: [...new Set(trustedOrigins)],
  emailAndPassword: {
    enabled: true,
    disableSignUp: process.env.ALLOW_ADMIN_SIGNUP === "false",
    // Password recovery revokes every existing session after the OTP is
    // consumed, so a stolen session cannot survive a recovery.
    revokeSessionsOnPasswordReset: true,
    onPasswordReset: async ({ user }) => {
      await logActivity({
        actorUserId: user.id,
        targetUserId: user.id,
        action: "user_password_reset",
        resourceType: "user",
        resourceId: user.id,
        metadata: { method: "email-otp", sessionsRevoked: true },
      });
    },
  },
  emailVerification: {
    afterEmailVerification: async (user) => {
      await logActivity({
        actorUserId: user.id,
        targetUserId: user.id,
        action: "user_email_verified",
        resourceType: "user",
        resourceId: user.id,
        metadata: { method: "email-otp" },
      });
    },
  },
  session: {
    expiresIn: 60 * 60 * 24 * 7,
    updateAge: 60 * 60 * 24,
  },
  user: {
    additionalFields: {
      // Server-managed only (`input: false`): a signup or profile-update
      // payload can never change the approval state. New rows default to
      // pending; migration 0002 backfilled the pre-existing users as approved.
      approvalStatus: {
        type: "string" as const,
        required: false,
        defaultValue: "pending",
        input: false,
      },
      deletedAt: {
        type: "date" as const,
        required: false,
        input: false,
      },
    },
  },
  plugins: [
    admin({
      adminRoles: ["admin"],
      defaultRole: "user",
      bannedUserMessage: BANNED_USER_MESSAGE,
    }),
    // OTP-based password recovery. Better Auth owns the lifecycle: hashed
    // storage, 5-minute expiry, three attempts, per-path rate limiting,
    // single-use consumption, and non-enumerating request responses.
    emailOTP({
      otpLength: OTP_LENGTH,
      expiresIn: OTP_EXPIRES_IN_SECONDS,
      allowedAttempts: OTP_ALLOWED_ATTEMPTS,
      storeOTP: "hashed",
      resendStrategy: "rotate",
      disableSignUp: true,
      rateLimit: {
        window: OTP_RESEND_COOLDOWN_SECONDS,
        max: 3,
      },
      sendVerificationOTP: async ({ email, otp, type }) => {
        const content = otpEmailContent(type, otp);
        await sendSecurityEmail({ to: email, ...content });
      },
    }),
  ],
  hooks: {
    after: createAuthMiddleware(async (ctx) => {
      // Audit only recovery requests for accounts that exist. Unknown emails
      // receive the same success response from Better Auth, so this check is
      // server-side and never changes the client-visible result.
      if (ctx.path !== "/email-otp/request-password-reset") return;
      const rawEmail = (ctx.body as { email?: unknown } | undefined)?.email;
      if (typeof rawEmail !== "string") return;
      const email = rawEmail.trim().toLowerCase();
      if (!email) return;

      const [row] = await db
        .select({ id: schema.user.id })
        .from(schema.user)
        .where(eq(schema.user.email, email))
        .limit(1);
      if (!row) return;

      await logActivity({
        actorUserId: row.id,
        targetUserId: row.id,
        action: "user_password_reset_requested",
        resourceType: "user",
        resourceId: row.id,
        metadata: { method: "email-otp" },
      });
    }),
  },
  databaseHooks: {
    user: {
      create: {
        // Server-side signup protection: whatever the client sends, every
        // freshly registered user is a regular pending user. Role changes are
        // reserved for the admin plugin's admin-only endpoints, and the
        // database's partial unique `role` index (migration 0002) guarantees
        // at most one admin row even under a misplaced call.
        before: async (user) => ({
          data: {
            ...user,
            role: "user",
            approvalStatus: "pending",
            banned: false,
            banReason: null,
            banExpires: null,
            deletedAt: null,
          },
        }),
        after: async (user) => {
          // Audit: registration creates a pending account that waits for admin
          // approval. The signup session is discarded right after creation.
          await logActivity({
            actorUserId: user.id,
            targetUserId: user.id,
            action: "user_signup_pending",
            resourceType: "user",
            resourceId: user.id,
            metadata: { approvalStatus: "pending" },
          });
        },
      },
    },
    session: {
      create: {
        // Soft-deleted users can never create a new session, even with valid
        // credentials or a replayed login request.
        before: async (session) => {
          const [user] = await db
            .select({ deletedAt: schema.user.deletedAt, banned: schema.user.banned })
            .from(schema.user)
            .where(eq(schema.user.id, session.userId))
            .limit(1);
          if (user?.deletedAt) return false;
          // Banned users are already rejected natively by the admin plugin
          // with BANNED_USER_MESSAGE; this is a belt-and-braces guard.
          if (user?.banned) return false;
          return undefined;
        },
        after: async (session) => {
          // Login audit. Only non-sensitive request context is stored: never
          // the session token, cookie, password, or headers.
          await logActivity({
            actorUserId: session.userId,
            targetUserId: session.userId,
            action: "user_login",
            resourceType: "session",
            resourceId: session.id,
            metadata: {
              ipAddress: session.ipAddress ?? null,
              userAgent: session.userAgent ? session.userAgent.slice(0, 200) : null,
            },
          });
        },
      },
    },
  },
});

export type AppUser = NonNullable<Awaited<ReturnType<typeof auth.api.getSession>>>["user"];

// Database error helpers. Kept separate from the query modules so they can be
// unit-tested without a database connection.

/**
 * True when the error, or anything in its `cause` chain, is a PostgreSQL
 * unique-violation (SQLSTATE 23505). Drizzle wraps driver errors in
 * `DrizzleQueryError`, so the SQLSTATE normally lives on `cause` rather than on
 * the thrown error itself. The depth cap also makes cyclic causes safe.
 */
export function isUniqueViolation(error: unknown, depth = 0): boolean {
  if (depth > 5 || typeof error !== "object" || error === null) return false;
  if ((error as { code?: unknown }).code === "23505") return true;
  return isUniqueViolation((error as { cause?: unknown }).cause, depth + 1);
}

import { drizzle } from "drizzle-orm/node-postgres";
import { Pool, type PoolClient, type PoolConfig } from "pg";

import { config } from "@/lib/backend";

import * as schema from "./schema";

const globalForDb = globalThis as unknown as { scheduledMediaDbPool?: Pool };

const POOL_MAX = 5;

function connectionString(): string {
  return (process.env.DATABASE_URL?.trim() || config.databaseUrl || "").trim();
}

// `pg` enables TLS only when the connection string itself carries an `sslmode`
// parameter; without one it connects in cleartext. Supabase does not currently
// reject unencrypted sessions, so a DATABASE_URL without `?sslmode=require`
// silently degrades to plaintext. Enforce encryption for Supabase hosts unless
// the URL explicitly configures TLS itself. `rejectUnauthorized: false` matches
// `sslmode=require` semantics (encryption required, no CA verification) so no
// CA bundle has to be shipped with the deployment.
function sslOverride(connectionUrl: string): PoolConfig["ssl"] {
  let parsed: URL;
  try {
    parsed = new URL(connectionUrl);
  } catch {
    return undefined;
  }
  if (parsed.protocol !== "postgres:" && parsed.protocol !== "postgresql:") return undefined;
  if (parsed.searchParams.has("sslmode")) return undefined;
  if (!/\.supabase\.(co|com)$/.test(parsed.hostname)) return undefined;
  return { rejectUnauthorized: false };
}

const connectionUrl = connectionString();

const pool = globalForDb.scheduledMediaDbPool ?? new Pool({
  connectionString: connectionUrl,
  ssl: sslOverride(connectionUrl),
  max: POOL_MAX,
  connectionTimeoutMillis: 10000,
  idleTimeoutMillis: 30000,
  keepAlive: true,
});

// `pg` emits `error` on the pool when an idle client's connection dies (for
// example Supabase closing an idle TCP connection with ECONNRESET). Without a
// listener that becomes an uncaughtException and takes down the server process
// / serverless invocation. Log it and let the pool establish a replacement,
// matching the backend pool in social-media-mcp/src/database.ts.
pool.on("error", (error: Error & { code?: string }) => {
  console.error(
    JSON.stringify({
      event: "database_pool_error",
      code: error.code ?? "UNKNOWN",
      message:
        "An idle PostgreSQL connection failed; the pool will establish a replacement as needed.",
    }),
  );
});

// A client that errors while CHECKED OUT of the pool (between `connect()` and
// `release()`, for example inside a Drizzle transaction when the server
// terminates the connection) has no pg-internal error listener: an
// EventEmitter `error` event with no listener throws an uncaughtException and
// kills the serverless invocation. Attach a permanent safety listener to every
// client; pg-pool's own idle/checkout handlers still run alongside it, and the
// dead client is removed from the pool on its eventual release because
// `client._queryable` is false after a connection error.
pool.on("connect", (client: PoolClient) => {
  client.on("error", (error: Error & { code?: string }) => {
    console.error(
      JSON.stringify({
        event: "database_client_error",
        code: error.code ?? "UNKNOWN",
        message: "A pooled PostgreSQL connection failed; it will be removed from the pool.",
      }),
    );
  });
});

// Transport-level failures: Node socket errors and PostgreSQL connection-state
// / resource-limit SQLSTATEs. Anything else (a failed query, an adapter bug)
// is not a connection problem and must not trigger pool recovery.
const CONNECTION_ERROR_CODES = new Set([
  "ECONNRESET",
  "ECONNREFUSED",
  "ECONNABORTED",
  "ETIMEDOUT",
  "EPIPE",
  "EHOSTUNREACH",
  "ENETUNREACH",
  "ENOTFOUND",
  "EAI_AGAIN",
  // connection_does_not_exist / sqlclient_unable_to_establish / etc.
  "08000",
  "08001",
  "08003",
  "08004",
  "08006",
  "08007",
  // too_many_connections / admin_shutdown / crash_shutdown / cannot_connect_now
  "53300",
  "57P01",
  "57P02",
  "57P03",
  "53400",
]);
const CONNECTION_ERROR_PATTERN =
  /connection (terminated|refused|reset|timed out|ended)|too many clients|terminating connection|server closed the connection|socket (connection )?closed/i;

export function isConnectionError(error: unknown): boolean {
  let current: unknown = error;
  for (let depth = 0; depth < 5 && current instanceof Error; depth += 1) {
    const code = (current as NodeJS.ErrnoException).code;
    if (typeof code === "string" && CONNECTION_ERROR_CODES.has(code)) return true;
    if (CONNECTION_ERROR_PATTERN.test(current.message)) return true;
    current = (current as { cause?: unknown }).cause;
  }
  return false;
}

// Serverless instances freeze between requests and providers (Supabase /
// Supavisor) close idle TCP connections while they are frozen. On the next
// request the pool hands out those dead clients one query at a time: the first
// query after a thaw can fail on up to `POOL_MAX` consecutive dead clients
// before reaching a healthy one, which is more than a single blind retry can
// recover from. Each failed probe removes exactly one dead client from the
// pool (`client.release(error)`), so this bounded loop deterministically ends
// with either a verified-healthy pooled connection or a genuine outage.
const PROBE_TIMEOUT_MS = 3000;
const DRAIN_DEADLINE_MS = 9000;

export async function ensureDatabaseConnection(): Promise<boolean> {
  const deadline = Date.now() + DRAIN_DEADLINE_MS;
  for (let attempt = 0; attempt <= POOL_MAX && Date.now() < deadline; attempt += 1) {
    let client: PoolClient;
    try {
      client = await pool.connect();
    } catch {
      // No connection could be obtained at all (connect timeout, connection
      // cap, pooler outage) - a real infrastructure failure, not a stale
      // socket.
      return false;
    }

    let timer: NodeJS.Timeout | undefined;
    const outcome = await Promise.race([
      client.query("SELECT 1").then(
        () => true,
        (error: unknown) => error,
      ),
      new Promise<"timeout">((resolve) => {
        timer = setTimeout(
          () => resolve("timeout"),
          Math.max(1000, Math.min(PROBE_TIMEOUT_MS, deadline - Date.now())),
        );
      }),
    ]);
    if (timer) clearTimeout(timer);

    if (outcome === true) {
      client.release();
      return true;
    }

    // Remove the unhealthy client from the pool and force-close its socket;
    // the abandoned query, if any, rejects into the race result above and any
    // late client error is absorbed by the pool `error` listener.
    client.release(new Error("database client probe failed"));
    try {
      // `pg`'s `end()` returns void or a Promise depending on overload.
      void Promise.resolve(client.end()).catch(() => {});
    } catch {
      // Already closed.
    }

    if (outcome === "timeout" || isConnectionError(outcome)) continue;
    return false;
  }
  return false;
}

if (process.env.NODE_ENV !== "production") {
  globalForDb.scheduledMediaDbPool = pool;
}

export const db = drizzle(pool, { schema });
export { pool };

import { randomUUID } from "node:crypto";

import { sql } from "drizzle-orm";
import { boolean, jsonb, pgTable, text, timestamp } from "drizzle-orm/pg-core";

export const user = pgTable("user", {
  id: text("id").primaryKey(),
  name: text("name").notNull(),
  email: text("email").notNull().unique(),
  emailVerified: boolean("email_verified").notNull().default(false),
  image: text("image"),
  createdAt: timestamp("created_at", { withTimezone: true }).notNull().defaultNow(),
  updatedAt: timestamp("updated_at", { withTimezone: true }).notNull().defaultNow(),
  // Better Auth admin plugin fields (single Super Admin: role = "admin").
  role: text("role").notNull().default("user"),
  banned: boolean("banned").notNull().default(false),
  banReason: text("ban_reason"),
  banExpires: timestamp("ban_expires", { withTimezone: true }),
  // Multi-user approval workflow: pending -> approved | rejected. Suspension
  // is expressed through `banned`; deletion through `deleted_at`.
  approvalStatus: text("approval_status").notNull().default("pending"),
  deletedAt: timestamp("deleted_at", { withTimezone: true }),
});

export const session = pgTable("session", {
  id: text("id").primaryKey(),
  expiresAt: timestamp("expires_at", { withTimezone: true }).notNull(),
  token: text("token").notNull().unique(),
  createdAt: timestamp("created_at", { withTimezone: true }).notNull().defaultNow(),
  updatedAt: timestamp("updated_at", { withTimezone: true }).notNull().defaultNow(),
  ipAddress: text("ip_address"),
  userAgent: text("user_agent"),
  userId: text("user_id").notNull().references(() => user.id, { onDelete: "cascade" }),
  // Better Auth admin plugin: user id set on sessions created via
  // impersonateUser / revokeUserImpersonation. Nullable: regular sessions
  // never have it. Server-managed only (plugin field `input: false`).
  impersonatedBy: text("impersonated_by"),
});

export const account = pgTable("account", {
  id: text("id").primaryKey(),
  accountId: text("account_id").notNull(),
  providerId: text("provider_id").notNull(),
  userId: text("user_id").notNull().references(() => user.id, { onDelete: "cascade" }),
  accessToken: text("access_token"),
  refreshToken: text("refresh_token"),
  idToken: text("id_token"),
  accessTokenExpiresAt: timestamp("access_token_expires_at", { withTimezone: true }),
  refreshTokenExpiresAt: timestamp("refresh_token_expires_at", { withTimezone: true }),
  scope: text("scope"),
  password: text("password"),
  createdAt: timestamp("created_at", { withTimezone: true }).notNull().defaultNow(),
  updatedAt: timestamp("updated_at", { withTimezone: true }).notNull().defaultNow(),
});

export const verification = pgTable("verification", {
  id: text("id").primaryKey(),
  identifier: text("identifier").notNull(),
  value: text("value").notNull(),
  expiresAt: timestamp("expires_at", { withTimezone: true }).notNull(),
  createdAt: timestamp("created_at", { withTimezone: true }).defaultNow(),
  updatedAt: timestamp("updated_at", { withTimezone: true }).defaultNow(),
});

// Activity / audit trail (created by migration 0002, mirrored by the MCP
// backend's migration 013 so both apps write the same shape). Writers must
// never store passwords, tokens, secrets, or encryption keys in metadata.
export const activityLog = pgTable("activity_log", {
  id: text("id")
    .primaryKey()
    // Application-level id generation keeps inserts simple and matches the
    // database DDL (id text PRIMARY KEY without a server-side default).
    .$defaultFn(() => randomUUID()),
  actorUserId: text("actor_user_id"),
  targetUserId: text("target_user_id"),
  action: text("action").notNull(),
  resourceType: text("resource_type").notNull(),
  resourceId: text("resource_id"),
  // The shared DDL (web migration 0002 and MCP migration 013) declares this
  // column as jsonb. Declaring it as text here made reads return a parsed
  // object and made ILIKE searches fail with `operator does not exist`.
  metadata: jsonb("metadata")
    .$type<Record<string, unknown>>()
    .notNull()
    .default(sql`'{}'::jsonb`),
  createdAt: timestamp("created_at", { withTimezone: true }).notNull().defaultNow(),
});

// Security email delivery for OTP-based account recovery. Two transports are
// supported without adding a dependency:
//   1. Resend (RESEND_API_KEY + EMAIL_FROM)
//   2. A generic HTTPS webhook (EMAIL_DELIVERY_URL + optional EMAIL_DELIVERY_TOKEN)
// If neither is configured the message is dropped with a warning. Delivery
// failures are swallowed so an attacker cannot distinguish a real account from
// an unknown email by watching for a 5xx response. OTP values are never logged.

import { OTP_EXPIRES_IN_SECONDS } from "@/lib/security-policy";

export type SecurityEmailType =
  | "sign-in"
  | "email-verification"
  | "forget-password"
  | "change-email";

export interface SecurityEmail {
  to: string;
  subject: string;
  text: string;
}

const RESEND_ENDPOINT = "https://api.resend.com/emails";

function appName(): string {
  return process.env.EMAIL_APP_NAME?.trim() || "Social Console";
}

function expiryMinutes(): number {
  return Math.max(1, Math.round(OTP_EXPIRES_IN_SECONDS / 60));
}

/**
 * Builds the subject and plain-text body for a security OTP. The OTP appears
 * only in the message body; it is never written to logs, audit metadata, or
 * the subject line.
 */
export function otpEmailContent(
  type: SecurityEmailType,
  otp: string,
): { subject: string; text: string } {
  const name = appName();
  const minutes = expiryMinutes();
  const footer = `This code expires in ${minutes} minutes. If you did not request it, you can ignore this email.`;

  switch (type) {
    case "forget-password":
      return {
        subject: `${name} password reset code`,
        text: `Your ${name} password reset code is ${otp}.\n\n${footer}\n\nFor your security, never share this code with anyone.`,
      };
    case "email-verification":
      return {
        subject: `${name} recovery email verification code`,
        text: `Your ${name} recovery email verification code is ${otp}.\n\n${footer}`,
      };
    case "sign-in":
      return {
        subject: `${name} sign-in code`,
        text: `Your ${name} sign-in code is ${otp}.\n\n${footer}`,
      };
    case "change-email":
      return {
        subject: `${name} email change code`,
        text: `Your ${name} email change code is ${otp}.\n\n${footer}`,
      };
  }
}

/**
 * Best-effort delivery. This function never throws: the caller is an auth
 * endpoint that must keep its non-enumerating success response even when the
 * mail provider is down or misconfigured.
 */
export async function sendSecurityEmail(message: SecurityEmail): Promise<void> {
  const apiKey = process.env.RESEND_API_KEY?.trim();
  const webhookUrl = process.env.EMAIL_DELIVERY_URL?.trim();

  try {
    if (apiKey) {
      const from = process.env.EMAIL_FROM?.trim()
        || "Social Console <onboarding@resend.dev>";
      const response = await fetch(RESEND_ENDPOINT, {
        method: "POST",
        headers: {
          authorization: `Bearer ${apiKey}`,
          "content-type": "application/json",
        },
        body: JSON.stringify({
          from,
          to: [message.to],
          subject: message.subject,
          text: message.text,
        }),
      });
      if (!response.ok) {
        // Status only: the response body can echo the message content.
        console.error(`[email] Resend delivery failed with status ${response.status}.`);
      }
      return;
    }

    if (webhookUrl) {
      const token = process.env.EMAIL_DELIVERY_TOKEN?.trim();
      const response = await fetch(webhookUrl, {
        method: "POST",
        headers: {
          "content-type": "application/json",
          ...(token ? { authorization: `Bearer ${token}` } : {}),
        },
        body: JSON.stringify({
          to: message.to,
          subject: message.subject,
          text: message.text,
        }),
      });
      if (!response.ok) {
        console.error(`[email] Webhook delivery failed with status ${response.status}.`);
      }
      return;
    }

    console.warn(
      "[email] Security email delivery is not configured (set RESEND_API_KEY or EMAIL_DELIVERY_URL); message was not sent.",
    );
  } catch (error) {
    // Never log the message body, recipient, or OTP.
    console.error(
      "[email] Security email delivery failed:",
      error instanceof Error ? error.message : "unknown error",
    );
  }
}

// Returns a safe same-origin path for post-login/post-signup navigation.
// Anything that could become an absolute or protocol-relative URL (for example
// `//evil.example`, `/\evil.example`, or encoded slashes) falls back to `/`.
export function safeRedirectPath(value: unknown, fallback = "/"): string {
  if (typeof value !== "string" || !value.startsWith("/")) return fallback;
  if (value.startsWith("//")) return fallback;

  // Only the path component can turn into an authority, so check it in
  // isolation and keep legitimate encoded characters in the query string.
  const pathPart = value.split(/[?#]/, 1)[0] ?? "";
  if (/[\\\u0000-\u001f\u007f]/.test(pathPart)) return fallback;
  if (/%5c|%2f/i.test(pathPart)) return fallback;

  try {
    const url = new URL(value, "http://localhost");
    if (url.origin !== "http://localhost") return fallback;
    return `${url.pathname}${url.search}${url.hash}`;
  } catch {
    return fallback;
  }
}

// Pure profile/password/OTP policy helpers. Kept free of database, auth, and
// Next.js imports so the same rules run in the browser form, the API route,
// the emergency recovery script, and unit tests.

export const DISPLAY_NAME_MIN_LENGTH = 2;
export const DISPLAY_NAME_MAX_LENGTH = 80;

export const PASSWORD_MIN_LENGTH = 12;
export const PASSWORD_MAX_LENGTH = 128;

export const OTP_LENGTH = 6;
export const OTP_EXPIRES_IN_SECONDS = 300;
export const OTP_ALLOWED_ATTEMPTS = 3;
export const OTP_RESEND_COOLDOWN_SECONDS = 60;

export type ValidationResult<T> =
  | { ok: true; value: T }
  | { ok: false; message: string };

const CONTROL_CHARACTERS = /[\u0000-\u001f\u007f]/;
const DISPLAY_NAME_PATTERN = /^[\p{L}\p{N} .,'’\-_()&]+$/u;

/**
 * Normalizes and validates the administrator display name. Names are only
 * presentation data; the role and email are never editable through this path.
 */
export function validateDisplayName(value: unknown): ValidationResult<string> {
  if (typeof value !== "string") {
    return { ok: false, message: "Name must be text." };
  }

  const name = value.trim().replace(/\s+/g, " ");
  if (name.length < DISPLAY_NAME_MIN_LENGTH) {
    return {
      ok: false,
      message: `Name must be at least ${DISPLAY_NAME_MIN_LENGTH} characters.`,
    };
  }
  if (name.length > DISPLAY_NAME_MAX_LENGTH) {
    return {
      ok: false,
      message: `Name must be at most ${DISPLAY_NAME_MAX_LENGTH} characters.`,
    };
  }
  if (CONTROL_CHARACTERS.test(name)) {
    return { ok: false, message: "Name contains unsupported characters." };
  }
  if (!DISPLAY_NAME_PATTERN.test(name)) {
    return {
      ok: false,
      message:
        "Name may contain letters, numbers, spaces, and common punctuation only.",
    };
  }

  return { ok: true, value: name };
}

export interface PasswordRequirements {
  length: boolean;
  lowercase: boolean;
  uppercase: boolean;
  digit: boolean;
  symbol: boolean;
}

export function passwordRequirements(value: string): PasswordRequirements {
  return {
    length: value.length >= PASSWORD_MIN_LENGTH && value.length <= PASSWORD_MAX_LENGTH,
    lowercase: /[a-z]/.test(value),
    uppercase: /[A-Z]/.test(value),
    digit: /\d/.test(value),
    symbol: /[^A-Za-z0-9]/.test(value),
  };
}

/**
 * Enforces a 12+ character password with at least three of four character
 * classes. This is intentionally stricter than Better Auth's built-in minimum
 * and is re-checked server-side before the provider is called.
 */
export function validatePasswordStrength(value: unknown): ValidationResult<string> {
  if (typeof value !== "string" || value.length === 0) {
    return { ok: false, message: "Password is required." };
  }
  if (value.length < PASSWORD_MIN_LENGTH) {
    return {
      ok: false,
      message: `Password must be at least ${PASSWORD_MIN_LENGTH} characters.`,
    };
  }
  if (value.length > PASSWORD_MAX_LENGTH) {
    return {
      ok: false,
      message: `Password must be at most ${PASSWORD_MAX_LENGTH} characters.`,
    };
  }
  if (CONTROL_CHARACTERS.test(value)) {
    return { ok: false, message: "Password contains unsupported characters." };
  }

  const requirements = passwordRequirements(value);
  const classes = [
    requirements.lowercase,
    requirements.uppercase,
    requirements.digit,
    requirements.symbol,
  ].filter(Boolean).length;

  if (classes < 3) {
    return {
      ok: false,
      message:
        "Password must include at least three of: lowercase, uppercase, numbers, symbols.",
    };
  }

  return { ok: true, value };
}

export interface PasswordChangeInput {
  currentPassword?: unknown;
  newPassword?: unknown;
  confirmPassword?: unknown;
}

export interface ValidatedPasswordChange {
  currentPassword: string;
  newPassword: string;
}

/**
 * Validates a self-service password change. The current password is only
 * checked for shape here; Better Auth verifies the real hash server-side.
 */
export function validatePasswordChange(
  input: PasswordChangeInput,
): ValidationResult<ValidatedPasswordChange> {
  const currentPassword = input.currentPassword;
  if (typeof currentPassword !== "string" || currentPassword.length === 0) {
    return { ok: false, message: "Current password is required." };
  }
  if (currentPassword.length > PASSWORD_MAX_LENGTH) {
    return { ok: false, message: "Current password is too long." };
  }

  const strength = validatePasswordStrength(input.newPassword);
  if (!strength.ok) return strength;

  if (typeof input.confirmPassword !== "string" || input.confirmPassword.length === 0) {
    return { ok: false, message: "Confirm the new password." };
  }
  if (strength.value !== input.confirmPassword) {
    return { ok: false, message: "The new passwords do not match." };
  }
  if (strength.value === currentPassword) {
    return { ok: false, message: "The new password must differ from the current password." };
  }

  return {
    ok: true,
    value: { currentPassword, newPassword: strength.value },
  };
}

/** Validates the 6-digit numeric OTP accepted by the email-OTP provider. */
export function validateOtp(value: unknown): ValidationResult<string> {
  if (typeof value !== "string") {
    return { ok: false, message: "Enter the 6-digit code from your email." };
  }
  const otp = value.trim();
  if (!new RegExp(`^\\d{${OTP_LENGTH}}$`).test(otp)) {
    return { ok: false, message: "Enter the 6-digit code from your email." };
  }
  return { ok: true, value: otp };
}

/** Lowercases and lightly validates an email before an OTP request. */
export function normalizeEmail(value: unknown): string | null {
  if (typeof value !== "string") return null;
  const email = value.trim().toLowerCase();
  if (email.length === 0 || email.length > 254) return null;
  if (!/^[^\s@]+@[^\s@]+\.[^\s@]+$/.test(email)) return null;
  return email;
}

FILE: social-media-web/src/lib/session.ts

import { cache } from "react";

import { headers } from "next/headers";
import { unstable_rethrow } from "next/navigation";

import { auth, ADMIN_ROLE, type AppUser } from "@/lib/auth";
import { ensureDatabaseConnection } from "@/lib/db";

export type AdminSession = NonNullable<Awaited<ReturnType<typeof auth.api.getSession>>>;

/**
 * Thrown when the session lookup itself fails (database unreachable, connection
 * pool exhausted, adapter error) as opposed to a session being absent, expired,
 * or invalid. Better Auth returns `null` for those cases and only throws an
 * `APIError` (`FAILED_TO_GET_SESSION`) when the lookup cannot be completed.
 *
 * Callers must not treat this as "signed out": an infrastructure outage must
 * never silently sign a user out or render the dashboard as unauthenticated.
 */
export class SessionUnavailableError extends Error {
  readonly status = 503;
  readonly code = "SESSION_UNAVAILABLE";

  constructor() {
    super("Your session could not be verified because the authentication service is temporarily unavailable.");
    this.name = "SessionUnavailableError";
  }
}

// Log only non-sensitive identifying fields. The underlying database error can
// carry the bound session token in its query parameters, so the cause is never
// logged or forwarded to the client.
function logSessionLookupFailure(error: unknown): void {
  const details =
    error instanceof Error
      ? {
          name: error.name,
          message: error.message
            .replace(/postgres(?:ql)?:\/\/[^\s"'<>]+/gi, "[database URL redacted]")
            .slice(0, 300),
          code: (error as { body?: { code?: unknown } }).body?.code,
        }
      : { name: typeof error };
  console.error(JSON.stringify({ event: "session_lookup_failed", ...details }));
}

// Better Auth wraps every failed session lookup in an opaque `APIError`
// (FAILED_TO_GET_SESSION); the underlying database error is only logged, never
// attached as a cause, so transient connection failures cannot be recognized
// from the thrown error alone. Live diagnosis against the production database
// confirmed the failure mode: serverless instances on Vercel freeze between
// requests, providers close the instance's idle TCP connections while it is
// frozen, and the pool then hands out those dead clients one query at a time -
// so a lookup can fail on several consecutive dead clients before reaching a
// healthy connection, which a single blind retry cannot recover from.
//
// Recovery is therefore deterministic, not a blind retry: verify (and drain
// dead clients from) the pool with `ensureDatabaseConnection`, then re-run the
// lookup exactly once. The second attempt re-runs the entire verification
// against the database - nothing is cached or assumed from the first attempt -
// so it can never fabricate a session. A persistent outage fails the retry too
// and still surfaces as `SessionUnavailableError`.

async function lookupSession(): Promise<AdminSession | null> {
  const result = await auth.api.getSession({ headers: await headers() });
  return result ?? null;
}

// `cache` deduplicates the lookup within a single render: the dashboard layout
// and the page (for example requireAdmin() on /admin) each call getSession(),
// and without dedupe every page render performs two or more full session
// lookups - each one another chance to hit a stale connection.
export const getSession = cache(async (): Promise<AdminSession | null> => {
  try {
    return await lookupSession();
  } catch (error) {
    // Never intercept Next.js control-flow errors (dynamic-usage from
    // `headers()`, redirect/notFound, prerender bailouts). They must reach the
    // framework; during `next build` they are how a route is marked dynamic.
    unstable_rethrow(error);
    logSessionLookupFailure(error);
    if (!(await ensureDatabaseConnection())) {
      throw new SessionUnavailableError();
    }
    try {
      return await lookupSession();
    } catch (retryError) {
      unstable_rethrow(retryError);
      logSessionLookupFailure(retryError);
      throw new SessionUnavailableError();
    }
  }
});

export class UnauthorizedError extends Error {
  constructor() {
    super("Authentication required.");
    this.name = "UnauthorizedError";
  }
}

export class ApprovalRequiredError extends Error {
  readonly status = 403;
  readonly code: "pending" | "rejected" | "suspended" | "deleted";

  constructor(code: ApprovalRequiredError["code"]) {
    const messages: Record<ApprovalRequiredError["code"], string> = {
      pending: "This account is awaiting administrator approval.",
      rejected: "This account was not approved. Contact the administrator if you believe this is a mistake.",
      suspended: "This account has been suspended. Contact the administrator if you believe this is a mistake.",
      deleted: "This account is no longer active.",
    };
    super(messages[code]);
    this.name = "ApprovalRequiredError";
    this.code = code;
  }
}

/** Outcome of the account-state check: either access or the deny reason. */
export type AccessDecision = "approved" | ApprovalRequiredError["code"];

export interface AccountState {
  role: string;
  isAdmin: boolean;
  approvalStatus: "pending" | "approved" | "rejected";
  banned: boolean;
  banActive: boolean;
  deleted: boolean;
}

// Better Auth returns the admin-plugin fields on the session user. Roles can
// be a comma-joined string or an array; parse defensively so authorization
// never depends on a specific plugin typing shape.
export function readAccountState(session: AdminSession | null): AccountState | null {
  if (!session) return null;
  const user = session.user as unknown as Record<string, unknown> & Pick<AppUser, "id">;
  const rawRole = user["role"];
  const roleParts = Array.isArray(rawRole)
    ? rawRole.map(String)
    : typeof rawRole === "string" ? rawRole.split(",").map((part) => part.trim()) : [];
  if (roleParts.length === 0) roleParts.push("user");
  const rawApproval = user["approvalStatus"];
  const approvalStatus = rawApproval === "approved" || rawApproval === "rejected" ? rawApproval : "pending";
  const banned = user["banned"] === true;
  const banExpiresAt = user["banExpires"] instanceof Date ? user["banExpires"] : null;
  const deletedAt = user["deletedAt"];
  return {
    role: roleParts[0]!,
    isAdmin: roleParts.includes(ADMIN_ROLE),
    approvalStatus,
    banned,
    banActive: banned && (banExpiresAt === null || banExpiresAt.getTime() > Date.now()),
    deleted: deletedAt instanceof Date && !Number.isNaN(deletedAt.getTime()),
  };
}

export function denyReason(state: AccountState): AccessDecision {
  if (state.deleted) return "deleted";
  if (state.banActive) return "suspended";
  if (state.approvalStatus !== "approved") return state.approvalStatus;
  // A banned flag with a stale expiry is treated as approved again.
  return "approved";
}

/** Verify that a valid authenticated session exists. */
export async function requireAuthenticatedUser(): Promise<AdminSession> {
  const session = await getSession();
  if (!session) throw new UnauthorizedError();
  return session;
}

/**
 * Verify the session user is an approved, unbanned, not soft-deleted account.
 * The Super Admin passes this check as well (admin accounts are approved).
 */
export async function requireApprovedUser(): Promise<AdminSession> {
  const session = await requireAuthenticatedUser();
  const state = readAccountState(session);
  if (!state) throw new UnauthorizedError();
  const reason = denyReason(state);
  if (reason !== "approved") throw new ApprovalRequiredError(reason);
  return session;
}

/**
 * Verify the session belongs to the single Super Admin. Regular users -
 * regardless of session validity - can never pass this check, and role
 * changes are only possible through admin-only endpoints backed by the
 * database-level single-admin unique index.
 */
export async function requireAdmin(): Promise<AdminSession> {
  const session = await requireAuthenticatedUser();
  const state = readAccountState(session);
  if (!state) throw new UnauthorizedError();
  if (!state.isAdmin) throw new ApprovalRequiredError("rejected");
  const reason = denyReason(state);
  if (reason !== "approved") throw new ApprovalRequiredError(reason);
  return session;
}

/**
 * Ownership guard: the authenticated user id always comes from the verified
 * server-side session; a client-supplied user id is never trusted. Compare it
 * against the resource owner when a request could address another user's data.
 */
export function requireResourceOwnership(session: AdminSession, ownerUserId: string): void {
  if (session.user.id !== ownerUserId) throw new ApprovalRequiredError("rejected");
}

FILE: social-media-web/src/lib/worker-throttle.ts

// Lightweight per-user cooldown for the "Run now" publishing trigger.
//
// The worker itself is already safe under concurrency (database row locks with
// FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED and `social_media_account_is_active`). This throttle
// only prevents an authenticated user from hammering the endpoint and creating
// pointless load. It is deliberately in-memory: it is a best-effort UX guard,
// not a security boundary.

const WINDOW_MS = 10_000;
const MAX_TRACKED_USERS = 1000;

const lastRunByUser = new Map<string, number>();

export interface WorkerSlot {
  allowed: boolean;
  retryAfterMs: number;
}

export function tryAcquireWorkerSlot(
  userId: string,
  now: number = Date.now(),
  windowMs: number = WINDOW_MS,
): WorkerSlot {
  const last = lastRunByUser.get(userId);
  if (last !== undefined && now - last < windowMs) {
    return { allowed: false, retryAfterMs: windowMs - (now - last) };
  }
  lastRunByUser.set(userId, now);
  if (lastRunByUser.size > MAX_TRACKED_USERS) {
    const cutoff = now - windowMs;
    for (const [id, timestamp] of lastRunByUser) {
      if (timestamp < cutoff) lastRunByUser.delete(id);
    }
  }
  return { allowed: true, retryAfterMs: 0 };
}

export function resetWorkerThrottleForTests(): void {
  lastRunByUser.clear();
}

export const WORKER_THROTTLE_WINDOW_MS = WINDOW_MS;

import { getSessionCookie } from "better-auth/cookies";
import { NextResponse, type NextRequest } from "next/server";

const PUBLIC_PREFIXES = [
  "/login",
  "/signup",
  "/pending",
  "/forgot-password",
  "/api/auth",
  "/api/health",
];

function isPublic(pathname: string): boolean {
  return PUBLIC_PREFIXES.some(
    (prefix) => pathname === prefix || pathname.startsWith(`${prefix}/`),
  );
}

export function proxy(request: NextRequest) {
  const { pathname } = request.nextUrl;
  const hasSession = Boolean(getSessionCookie(request));

  if (isPublic(pathname)) {
    return NextResponse.next();
  }

  if (!hasSession) {
    if (pathname.startsWith("/api")) {
      return Response.json({ error: "Authentication required." }, { status: 401 });
    }
    const url = request.nextUrl.clone();
    const next = `${pathname}${request.nextUrl.search}`;
    url.pathname = "/login";
    url.search = "";
    if (pathname !== "/" || request.nextUrl.search) url.searchParams.set("next", next);
    return NextResponse.redirect(url);
  }

  return NextResponse.next();
}

export const config = {
  matcher: [
    "/((?!_next/static|_next/image|favicon.ico|.*\\.(?:png|jpg|jpeg|gif|svg|ico|webp|woff|woff2|pdf)$).*)",
  ],
};

@utility shimmer {
  --_spread: var(--shimmer-spread, calc(3ch + 40px));
  --_base: currentColor;
  --_highlight: var(
    --shimmer-color,
    oklch(from currentColor l c h / calc(alpha* 0.2))
  );

  background-image: var(
    --shimmer-image,
    linear-gradient(
      calc(90deg + var(--shimmer-angle)),
      var(--_base) calc(50% - var(--_spread)),
      color-mix(in oklch, var(--_highlight), var(--_base) 50%)
        calc(50% - var(--_spread) * 0.5),
      var(--_highlight) 50%,
      color-mix(in oklch, var(--_highlight), var(--_base) 50%)
        calc(50% + var(--_spread) * 0.5),
      var(--_base) calc(50% + var(--_spread))
    )
  );
  background-repeat: no-repeat;
  background-size: calc(200% + var(--_spread) * 2) 100%;
  background-position: 0 0;
  background-clip: text;
  -webkit-background-clip: text;
  -webkit-text-fill-color: var(--shimmer-text-fill, transparent);
  animation: tw-shimmer var(--shimmer-duration, 2s) linear infinite;

  @variant dark {
    --_highlight: var(
      --shimmer-color,
      oklch(from currentColor max(0.8, calc(l + 0.4)) c h / calc(alpha + 0.4))
    );

FILE: social-media-web/tests/accounts-unified.test.ts

import { readFileSync } from "node:fs";

import { describe, expect, it } from "vitest";

import { accountConnectionState, connectionAction } from "@/lib/account-connection-state";

const readFile = (relative: string) => readFileSync(relative, "utf8");

const page = readFile("src/app/(dashboard)/accounts/page.tsx");
const panel = readFile("src/app/(dashboard)/accounts/accounts-panel.tsx");
const credentialsRoute = readFile("src/app/api/credentials/route.ts");
const platformsRoute = readFile("src/app/api/platforms/route.ts");
const appCredentials = readFile("../social-media-mcp/src/auth/app-credentials.ts");
const oauth = readFile("../social-media-mcp/src/auth/oauth.ts");
const linkedin = readFile("../social-media-mcp/src/platforms/linkedin.ts");
const migration = readFile("../social-media-mcp/migrations/009_user_app_credentials.sql");

describe("accountConnectionState", () => {
  it("treats a missing or disconnected status as disconnected", () => {
    expect(accountConnectionState(undefined)).toBe("disconnected");
    expect(accountConnectionState({ connected: false })).toBe("disconnected");
  });

  it("only reports connected for a live, unexpired authorization", () => {
    expect(accountConnectionState({ connected: true })).toBe("connected");
    expect(accountConnectionState({ connected: true, tokenExpired: false })).toBe(
      "connected",
    );
    expect(accountConnectionState({ connected: true, tokenExpired: true })).toBe(
      "expired",
    );
  });
});

describe("connectionAction (Connect vs Reconnect)", () => {
  it("shows Connect for users who never completed an OAuth consent", () => {
    expect(connectionAction("disconnected")).toBe("connect");
    expect(connectionAction("disconnected", false)).toBe("connect");
  });

  it("shows Connect when only developer app credentials are saved", () => {
    // Saved credentials must not imply a previous social account connection;
    // the panel passes the API's token-record flag, not credential state.
    expect(connectionAction("disconnected", false)).toBe("connect");
  });

  it("shows Reconnect when a previous connection exists but is no longer active", () => {
    expect(connectionAction("expired", true)).toBe("reconnect");
    expect(connectionAction("disconnected", true)).toBe("reconnect");
  });

  it("shows Reconnect for a currently connected platform as its management action", () => {
    expect(connectionAction("connected")).toBe("reconnect");
    expect(connectionAction("connected", true)).toBe("reconnect");
  });

  it("defaults to Connect when the API response carries no history flag", () => {
    expect(connectionAction("disconnected", undefined)).toBe("connect");
  });
});

describe("unified Accounts page", () => {
  it("renders one AccountsPanel and no duplicate developer settings section", () => {
    expect(page).toMatch(/<AccountsPanel \/>/);
    expect(page).not.toMatch(/DeveloperAppSettings/);
    expect(page.match(/<AccountsPanel \/>/g)).toHaveLength(1);
  });

  it("loads both live connection state and saved credential metadata", () => {
    expect(panel).toMatch(/fetch\("\/api\/platforms", \{ cache: "no-store" \}\)/);
    expect(panel).toMatch(/fetch\("\/api\/credentials", \{ cache: "no-store" \}\)/);
    expect(panel).toMatch(/accountConnectionState\(connection\)/);
  });

  it("keeps one card per provider with credentials and connection actions together", () => {
    for (const provider of ["facebook", "instagram", "linkedin"]) {
      expect(panel).toContain(`  ${provider}: {`);
    }
    expect(panel).toMatch(/PLATFORM_ORDER: PlatformId\[\] = \["facebook", "instagram", "linkedin"\]/);
    expect(panel).toContain("Save credentials");
    expect(panel).toContain("Update credentials");
    expect(panel).toContain("Connect");
    expect(panel).toContain("Reconnect");
    expect(panel).toContain("Credentials saved");
    expect(panel).toContain("type=\"password\"");
  });

  it("drives the card border from the connection state, never from saved credentials", () => {
    expect(panel).toMatch(/cardRingClass\(state\)/);
    expect(panel).toContain("ring-emerald-500/80");
    expect(panel).toContain("ring-amber-500/70");
    expect(panel).toContain("bg-emerald-600 text-white");
  });

  it("never stores credentials in browser storage", () => {
    expect(panel).not.toMatch(/localStorage|sessionStorage|document\.cookie/);
  });

  it("never reads or renders a secret returned by the API", () => {
    const credentialInterface = panel.slice(
      panel.indexOf("interface CredentialStatus"),
      panel.indexOf("interface ProviderMeta"),
    );
    expect(credentialInterface).toContain("clientId?: string");
    expect(credentialInterface).not.toContain("clientSecret");
    expect(panel).not.toMatch(/credential\.clientSecret|credentialsBody\.clientSecret/);
    expect(panel).toMatch(/Leave blank to keep the saved secret/);
  });
});

describe("credential storage and isolation", () => {
  it("stores only an AES-256-GCM envelope bound to the owner and provider", () => {
    expect(migration).toMatch(/client_secret_ciphertext JSONB NOT NULL/);
    expect(migration).not.toMatch(/client_secret\s+TEXT/i);
    expect(appCredentials).toMatch(/createCipheriv\("aes-256-gcm"/);
    expect(appCredentials).toMatch(/setAAD\(appSecretAad\(userId, provider\)\)/);
    expect(appCredentials).toContain(
      "social-media-mcp:app-credential:${userId}:${provider}:v1",
    );
  });

  it("scopes reads, updates, and deletes to the authenticated user", () => {
    expect(appCredentials).toMatch(
      /WHERE user_id = \$1 AND provider = \$2/,
    );
    expect(appCredentials).toMatch(
      /SET client_id = \$3, updated_at = NOW\(\) WHERE user_id = \$1 AND provider = \$2/,
    );
    expect(appCredentials).toMatch(
      /DELETE FROM public\.oauth_app_credentials WHERE user_id = \$1 AND provider = \$2/,
    );
    expect(credentialsRoute).toMatch(/session\.user\.id/);
  });

  it("preserves the existing secret when an update omits it", () => {
    expect(appCredentials).toMatch(
      /if \(clientSecret\) \{/,
    );
    expect(appCredentials).toContain("A blank secret preserves the stored one");
    expect(credentialsRoute).toMatch(/clientSecret: z\.string\(\)\.optional\(\)/);
    expect(credentialsRoute).toMatch(/if \(!configured && !\(clientSecret \?\? ""\)\.trim\(\)\)/);
  });

  it("returns only safe status metadata from the credentials API", () => {
    const statusInterface = appCredentials.slice(
      appCredentials.indexOf("export interface AppCredentialStatus"),
      appCredentials.indexOf("export interface ResolvedAppCredentials"),
    );
    expect(statusInterface).toContain("clientId?: string");
    expect(statusInterface).not.toContain("clientSecret");
    expect(credentialsRoute).toMatch(/appCredentialStatuses\(session\.user\.id\)/);
    expect(credentialsRoute).not.toMatch(/decryptAppSecret|client_secret_ciphertext/);
  });

  it("does not delete social tokens when app credentials are removed", () => {
    expect(appCredentials).toContain(
      "Deleting credentials only removes the app configuration.",
    );
    expect(appCredentials).not.toMatch(
      /DELETE FROM public\.oauth_tokens|saveTokens\(/,
    );
  });
});

describe("connection history detection", () => {
  it("derives the Connect/Reconnect flag from stored token records only", () => {
    // The platforms route merges per-user token metadata, which exists only
    // after a completed OAuth consent; saved developer credentials are a
    // separate table and must never produce the history flag.
    expect(platformsRoute).toMatch(/loadTokenMetadata\(session\.user\.id\)/);
    expect(platformsRoute).toMatch(/previouslyConnected: true/);
    expect(platformsRoute).not.toMatch(/appCredentialStatuses|loadAppCredentials/);
  });

  it("labels the card action via the shared truth table", () => {
    expect(panel).toMatch(
      /connectionAction\(state, connection\.previouslyConnected\)/,
    );
    expect(panel).toMatch(/action === "reconnect" \?/);
  });
});

describe("automatic credential reuse", () => {
  it("resolves the acting user's app for authorization start and token exchange", () => {
    expect(oauth).toMatch(
      /resolveAppCredentials\(userId, platform, \{\s*includeSecret: config\.oauthCallbackMode !== "cloud"/,
    );
    expect(oauth).toMatch(/resolveAppCredentials\(userId, platform\)/);
    expect(oauth).toContain("appCredentialFingerprint: credentials.fingerprint");
    expect(oauth).toContain("assertAppCredentialFingerprint");
  });

  it("refreshes LinkedIn tokens with the same user's app", () => {
    expect(linkedin).toMatch(
      /\(userId\) => resolveAppCredentials\(userId, "linkedin"\)/,
    );
    expect(linkedin).toContain("Refresh must use the LinkedIn app that issued the refresh token");
  });

  it("enriches status responses with display metadata without exposing tokens", () => {
    expect(platformsRoute).toMatch(/loadTokenMetadata\(session\.user\.id\)/);
    expect(platformsRoute).toContain("accountName");
    expect(platformsRoute).toContain("expiresAt");
    expect(platformsRoute).not.toMatch(/accessToken|refreshToken|token_ciphertext/);
  });
});

import { readFileSync } from "node:fs";
import path from "node:path";

import { describe, expect, it } from "vitest";

import {
  classifyUserStatus,
  isActiveAccount,
  type UserStatusRow,
} from "@/lib/admin-user-status";
import {
  summarizeUserStats,
  type UserStatsRow,
} from "@/lib/admin-overview-policy";

const readFile = (relative: string) =>
  readFileSync(path.resolve(process.cwd(), relative), "utf8");

function row(overrides: Partial<UserStatsRow> = {}): UserStatsRow {
  return {
    approvalStatus: "pending",
    banned: false,
    deleted: false,
    total: 1,
    ...overrides,
  };
}

describe("admin overview user statistics", () => {
  it("counts a newly registered pending user", () => {
    expect(summarizeUserStats([row()])).toMatchObject({
      total: 1,
      pending: 1,
      active: 0,
      inactive: 0,
    });
  });

  it("counts approved, unbanned users as active", () => {
    expect(
      summarizeUserStats([row({ approvalStatus: "approved" })]),
    ).toMatchObject({
      total: 1,
      pending: 0,
      active: 1,
      inactive: 0,
    });
  });

  it("counts rejected users as inactive", () => {
    expect(
      summarizeUserStats([row({ approvalStatus: "rejected" })]),
    ).toMatchObject({
      total: 1,
      pending: 0,
      active: 0,
      inactive: 1,
    });
  });

  it("counts banned users as inactive even when approval is approved or pending", () => {
    expect(
      summarizeUserStats([
        row({ approvalStatus: "approved", banned: true }),
        row({ approvalStatus: "pending", banned: true }),
      ]),
    ).toMatchObject({
      total: 2,
      pending: 0,
      active: 0,
      inactive: 2,
    });
  });

  it("counts soft-deleted users as inactive, including rejected users", () => {
    expect(
      summarizeUserStats([
        row({ approvalStatus: "rejected", deleted: true }),
        row({ approvalStatus: "approved", deleted: true }),
      ]),
    ).toMatchObject({
      total: 2,
      pending: 0,
      active: 0,
      inactive: 2,
    });
  });

  it("aggregates multiple users with different statuses without double counting", () => {
    const stats = summarizeUserStats([
      row({ approvalStatus: "approved", total: 3 }),
      row({ approvalStatus: "pending", total: 2 }),
      row({ approvalStatus: "rejected", total: 4 }),
      row({ approvalStatus: "approved", banned: true, total: 1 }),
      row({ approvalStatus: "pending", deleted: true, total: 1 }),
    ]);

    expect(stats).toEqual({
      total: 11,
      pending: 2,
      active: 3,
      inactive: 6,
    });
    expect(stats.pending + stats.active + stats.inactive).toBe(stats.total);
  });

  it("reflects status changes because each summary is derived from current rows", () => {
    const before = summarizeUserStats([row({ approvalStatus: "pending" })]);
    const after = summarizeUserStats([row({ approvalStatus: "approved" })]);

    expect(before).toMatchObject({ total: 1, pending: 1, active: 0 });
    expect(after).toMatchObject({ total: 1, pending: 0, active: 1 });
  });

  it("matches the requested counts after Super Admin rows are excluded", () => {
    // These are the rows PostgreSQL returns once `role <> 'admin'` is applied:
    // two approved normal users, one pending normal user, and one rejected,
    // soft-deleted normal user.
    const stats = summarizeUserStats([
      row({ approvalStatus: "approved" }),
      row({ approvalStatus: "approved" }),
      row({ approvalStatus: "pending" }),
      row({ approvalStatus: "rejected", deleted: true }),
    ]);

    expect(stats).toMatchObject({
      total: 4,
      pending: 1,
      active: 2,
      inactive: 1,
    });
  });
});

describe("user status classification", () => {
  const cases: [string, UserStatusRow, string][] = [
    [
      "a pending, active account",
      { approvalStatus: "pending", banned: false, deleted: false },
      "pending",
    ],
    [
      "an approved, active account",
      { approvalStatus: "approved", banned: false, deleted: false },
      "active",
    ],
    [
      "a rejected account",
      { approvalStatus: "rejected", banned: false, deleted: false },
      "inactive",
    ],
    [
      "a banned approved account",
      { approvalStatus: "approved", banned: true, deleted: false },
      "inactive",
    ],
    [
      "a banned pending account",
      { approvalStatus: "pending", banned: true, deleted: false },
      "inactive",
    ],
    [
      "a soft-deleted approved account",
      { approvalStatus: "approved", banned: false, deleted: true },
      "inactive",
    ],
    [
      "a rejected, soft-deleted account",
      { approvalStatus: "rejected", banned: false, deleted: true },
      "inactive",
    ],
    [
      "a soft-deleted pending account",
      { approvalStatus: "pending", banned: false, deleted: true },
      "inactive",
    ],
  ];

  it.each(cases)("classifies %s as %s", (_label, input, expected) => {
    expect(classifyUserStatus(input)).toBe(expected);
  });

  it("treats only unbanned, non-deleted accounts as active accounts", () => {
    expect(isActiveAccount({ banned: false, deleted: false })).toBe(true);
    expect(isActiveAccount({ banned: true, deleted: false })).toBe(false);
    expect(isActiveAccount({ banned: false, deleted: true })).toBe(false);
  });
});

describe("admin overview data source and UI", () => {
  const lib = readFile("src/lib/admin-overview.ts");
  const policy = readFile("src/lib/admin-overview-policy.ts");
  const statusPolicy = readFile("src/lib/admin-user-status.ts");
  const page = readFile("src/app/(dashboard)/admin/page.tsx");
  const route = readFile("src/app/api/admin/overview/route.ts");
  const usersLib = readFile("src/lib/admin-users.ts");
  const filtersLib = readFile("src/lib/admin-user-filters.ts");

  it("aggregates in PostgreSQL instead of loading users into memory", () => {
    expect(lib).toMatch(/\.groupBy\(/);
    expect(lib).toMatch(/count\(\)/);
    expect(lib).not.toMatch(/loadTokenMetadata/);
    expect(lib).not.toMatch(/scheduled_posts/);
    expect(lib).not.toMatch(/\.select\(\)\s*\.from\(user\)/);
  });

  it("uses one shared classifier instead of ad-hoc buckets", () => {
    expect(policy).toMatch(/classifyUserStatus/);
    expect(statusPolicy).toMatch(/export function classifyUserStatus/);
    expect(statusPolicy).toMatch(/row\.approvalStatus === "rejected"/);
    expect(statusPolicy).toMatch(/row\.approvalStatus === "pending"/);
    expect(statusPolicy).toMatch(/!row\.banned && !row\.deleted/);
  });

  it("shares the status rule with the Users directory", () => {
    expect(filtersLib).toMatch(/export function userStatusCondition/);
    expect(filtersLib).toMatch(/eq\(user\.approvalStatus, "pending"\)/);
    expect(filtersLib).toMatch(/eq\(user\.approvalStatus, "approved"\)/);
    expect(filtersLib).toMatch(/eq\(user\.approvalStatus, "rejected"\)/);
    expect(filtersLib).toMatch(/eq\(user\.banned, false\)/);
    expect(filtersLib).toMatch(/isNotNull\(user\.deletedAt\)/);
    expect(usersLib).toMatch(/userStatusCondition\(filters\.status\)/);
    expect(usersLib).toMatch(/getAdminUserStats\(\)/);
    expect(usersLib).toMatch(/total:\s*stats\.total/);
    expect(usersLib).toMatch(/pending:\s*stats\.pending/);
    expect(usersLib).toMatch(/active:\s*stats\.active/);
    expect(usersLib).toMatch(/inactive:\s*stats\.inactive/);
    expect(usersLib).not.toMatch(/groupBy\(user\.approvalStatus\)/);
  });

  it("shows only the four requested user statistics", () => {
    for (const label of [
      "Total Users",
      "Pending Users",
      "Active Users",
      "Inactive Users",
    ]) {
      expect(page).toContain(label);
    }

    expect(page).not.toContain("Approved Users");
    expect(page).not.toContain("Rejected Users");
    expect(page).not.toContain("Pending / On Hold");
    expect(page).not.toContain("On Hold");

    for (const href of [
      'href: "/users"',
      'href: "/users?status=pending"',
      'href: "/users?status=active"',
      'href: "/users?status=inactive"',
    ]) {
      expect(page).toContain(href);
    }
  });

  it("uses Active and Inactive labels in the directory and detail pages", () => {
    const table = readFile("src/app/(dashboard)/users/users-table.tsx");
    const detail = readFile("src/app/(dashboard)/users/[id]/page.tsx");
    const directoryFilters = readFile(
      "src/app/(dashboard)/users/users-filters.tsx",
    );

    expect(table).toContain("Active");
    expect(table).toContain("Inactive");
    expect(table).not.toContain(">Approved<");
    expect(table).not.toContain(">Rejected<");
    expect(detail).toContain("Inactive");
    expect(detail).not.toContain(">Rejected<");
    expect(directoryFilters).toContain('active: "Active"');
    expect(directoryFilters).toContain('inactive: "Inactive"');
    expect(directoryFilters).not.toContain('approved: "Approved"');
    expect(directoryFilters).not.toContain('rejected: "Rejected"');
  });

  it("removes the old dashboard sections and data sources", () => {
    for (const removed of [
      "DateRangeFilter",
      "OverviewChart",
      "Scheduled posts",
      "Published posts",
      "Failed posts",
      "Held posts",
      "Connected social accounts",
      "Suspended accounts",
      "Daily activity",
      "Recent activity",
      "Publishing snapshot",
      "Account health",
      "listActivity",
      "getAdminOverview",
    ]) {
      expect(page).not.toContain(removed);
    }
  });

  it("keeps the Super Admin guard and API error handling", () => {
    expect(page).toMatch(/requireAdminPage\(\)/);
    expect(route).toMatch(/await requireAdmin\(\)/);
    expect(route).toMatch(/apiErrorResponse\(error\)/);
  });
});

import { describe, expect, it } from "vitest";

import {
  groupConnectionsByOwner,
  type AdminSocialConnectionRow,
} from "@/lib/admin-social-grouping";

function connection(
  overrides: Partial<AdminSocialConnectionRow> = {},
): AdminSocialConnectionRow {
  return {
    userId: "user-1",
    userName: "Shriram",
    userEmail: "shriram@example.com",
    userStatus: "approved",
    platform: "facebook",
    status: "connected",
    accountName: "Shriram",
    accountId: "fb-1",
    expiresAt: null,
    expired: false,
    scopes: [],
    pageCount: 0,
    connectedAt: null,
    lastSyncAt: null,
    lastError: null,
    lastErrorAt: null,
    ...overrides,
  };
}

describe("groupConnectionsByOwner", () => {
  it("collapses three platforms for one owner into a single row", () => {
    const rows = groupConnectionsByOwner([
      connection({ platform: "linkedin", accountName: "Shriram LI" }),
      connection({ platform: "facebook", accountName: "Shriram FB" }),
      connection({ platform: "instagram", accountName: "IG account" }),
    ]);

    expect(rows).toHaveLength(1);
    expect(rows[0].userId).toBe("user-1");
    expect(rows[0].connections.map((row) => row.platform)).toEqual([
      "facebook",
      "instagram",
      "linkedin",
    ]);
  });

  it("keeps distinct owners separate even when names or emails collide", () => {
    const rows = groupConnectionsByOwner([
      connection({ userId: "user-1" }),
      connection({
        userId: "user-2",
        platform: "instagram",
        accountName: "Second account",
      }),
    ]);

    expect(rows.map((row) => row.userId)).toEqual(["user-1", "user-2"]);
    expect(rows[0].connections).toHaveLength(1);
    expect(rows[1].connections).toHaveLength(1);
  });

  it("preserves each platform's metadata without merging values", () => {
    const rows = groupConnectionsByOwner([
      connection({
        platform: "facebook",
        accountName: "FB name",
        status: "connected",
        lastSyncAt: "2026-01-01T10:00:00.000Z",
        expiresAt: "2026-02-01T10:00:00.000Z",
      }),
      connection({
        platform: "instagram",
        accountName: "IG name",
        status: "expired",
        expired: true,
        lastSyncAt: "2026-01-02T10:00:00.000Z",
        lastError: "Token expired",
      }),
    ]);

    expect(rows).toHaveLength(1);
    expect(rows[0].connections).toHaveLength(2);
    expect(rows[0].connections[0]).toMatchObject({
      platform: "facebook",
      accountName: "FB name",
      status: "connected",
      expiresAt: "2026-02-01T10:00:00.000Z",
    });
    expect(rows[0].connections[1]).toMatchObject({
      platform: "instagram",
      accountName: "IG name",
      status: "expired",
      expired: true,
      lastError: "Token expired",
    });
  });

  it("preserves owner order and handles empty input", () => {
    const rows = groupConnectionsByOwner([
      connection({ userId: "user-2", userEmail: "b@example.com" }),
      connection({
        userId: "user-1",
        userEmail: "a@example.com",
        platform: "linkedin",
      }),
      connection({
        userId: "user-2",
        userEmail: "b@example.com",
        platform: "instagram",
      }),
    ]);

    expect(rows.map((row) => row.userId)).toEqual(["user-2", "user-1"]);
    expect(rows[1].connections.map((row) => row.platform)).toEqual(["linkedin"]);
    expect(groupConnectionsByOwner([])).toEqual([]);
  });
});

FILE: social-media-web/tests/admin-users.test.ts
